data.title: A faster way to copy SQLite databases between computers
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种更快速在计算机间复制大型SQLite数据库的方法。随着数据库增长，直接使用`rsync`复制变得缓慢且不可靠。作者发现索引导致数据库文件变大，复制效率低。通过使用SQLite的`.dump`命令，将数据库导出为文本文件，可以显著缩小文件体积，因为索引被转化为创建指令而非实际数据。导出的文本文件还可以通过gzip压缩，进一步减小体积。新的复制流程包括在服务器上创建gzip压缩的文本文件，然后使用`rsync`复制到本地，最后解压并重建数据库。此方法不仅加快了复制速度，还确保了数据库的一致性，避免了复制过程中数据库被更新导致的文件损坏问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SQLite数据库备份与同步的方法及其效率优化

不同观点：
• **使用VACUUM INTO进行备份**：M95D认为使用`VACUUM INTO`命令备份SQLite数据库是高效的，可以减少文件系统I/O，并且备份文件体积最小化。
• **rsync的问题**：bambax指出直接使用rsync复制正在更新的数据库会导致文件损坏，因为更新过程中复制会导致文件前后不一致。他推荐使用Litestream来安全地复制SQLite数据库。
• **SQL语句传输与数据库传输的对比**：zeroq认为通过发送SQL语句来重建数据库并不一定比直接传输数据库更快，因为执行SQL语句还需要额外的时间和优化步骤（如执行/optimize/和/vacuum/）。
• **sqlite_rsync工具的优势**：hundredwatt提到新发布的sqlite_rsync工具使用优化的rsync算法来比较SQLite数据库的内部数据页，从而只同步更改或缺失的页，提高效率。
• **使用压缩**：mromanuk建议使用rsync的压缩功能（如-z和--compress-level）来加快传输速度，并指出压缩传输可以进一步优化。

补充讨论：
• **其他数据库技术**：simlevesque提到DuckDB可以将数据导出为Parquet格式，使得数据体积更小，传输和加载速度更快。RenThraysk提到SQLite的session扩展可以跟踪表的更改并生成补丁集。
• **实用工具和方法**：ollybee和markhahn提到SQLite提供的sqlite3_rsync命令用于安全复制数据库。markhahn还讨论了通过SSH直接传输SQL dump文件的可能性，并指出监测rsync检测到的更改量可能是有用的。
• **争议焦点**：主要争议在于使用SQL语句传输和直接传输数据库文件的效率对比，以及rsync在处理SQLite数据库同步时的可靠性和优化方法。

总的来说，讨论围绕着SQLite数据库的备份和同步方法展开，参与者提出了不同的工具和技巧以提高效率和可靠性。

43856186.article_content:
A faster way to copy SQLite databases between computers
Tagged with
sqlite
Posted
29 April 2025
I store a lot of data in SQLite databases on remote servers, and I often want to copy them to my local machine for analysis or backup.
When I’m starting a new project and the database is near-empty, this is a simple rsync operation:
$
rsync
--progress
username@server:my_remote_database.db my_local_database.db
As the project matures and the database grows, this gets slower and less reliable. Downloading a 250MB database from my web server takes about a minute over my home Internet connection, and that’s pretty small – most of my databases are multiple gigabytes in size.
I’ve been trying to make these copies go faster, and I recently discovered a neat trick.
What really slows me down is my indexes. I have a lot of indexes in my SQLite databases, which dramatically speed up my queries, but also make the database file larger and slower to copy. (In one database, there’s an index which single-handedly accounts for half the size on disk!)
The indexes don’t store anything unique – they just duplicate data from other tables to make queries faster. Copying the indexes makes the transfer less efficient, because I’m copying the same data multiple times. I was thinking about ways to skip copying the indexes, and I realised that SQLite has built-in tools to make this easy.
Dumping a database as a text file
SQLite allows you to
dump a database as a text file
. If you use the
.dump
command, it prints the entire database as a series of SQL statements. This text file can often be significantly smaller than the original database.
Here’s the command:
$
sqlite3 my_database.db .dump
>
my_database.db.txt
And here’s what the beginning of that file looks like:
PRAGMA
foreign_keys
=
OFF
;
BEGIN
TRANSACTION
;
CREATE
TABLE
IF
NOT
EXISTS
"tags"
(
[
name
]
TEXT
PRIMARY
KEY
,
[
count_uses
]
INTEGER
NOT
NULL
);
INSERT
INTO
tags
VALUES
(
'carving'
,
260
);
INSERT
INTO
tags
VALUES
(
'grass'
,
743
);
…
Crucially, this reduces the large and disk-heavy indexes into a single line of text – it’s an instruction to create an index, not the index itself.
CREATE
INDEX
[
idx_photo_locations
]
ON
[
photos
]
([
longitude
],
[
latitude
]);
This means that I’m only storing each value once, rather than the many times it may be stored across the original table and my indexes. This is how the text file can be smaller than the original database.
If you want to reconstruct the database, you pipe this text file back to SQLite:
$
cat
my_database.db.txt | sqlite3 my_reconstructed_database.db
Because the SQL statements are very repetitive, this text responds well to compression:
$
sqlite3 explorer.db .dump |
gzip
-c
>
explorer.db.txt.gz
To give you an idea of the potential savings, here’s the relative disk size for one of my databases.
File
Size on disk
original SQLite database
3.4 GB
text file (
sqlite3 my_database.db .dump
)
1.3 GB
gzip-compressed text (
sqlite3 my_database.db .dump | gzip -c
)
240 MB
The gzip-compressed text file is 14× smaller than the original SQLite database – that makes downloading the database much faster.
My new ssh+rsync command
Rather than copying the database directly, now I create a gzip-compressed text file on the server, copy that to my local machine, and reconstruct the database. Like so:
# Create a gzip-compressed text file on the server
ssh username@server
"sqlite3 my_remote_database.db .dump | gzip -c > my_remote_database.db.txt.gz"
# Copy the gzip-compressed text file to my local machine
rsync
--progress
username@server:my_remote_database.db.txt.gz my_local_database.db.txt.gz
# Remove the gzip-compressed text file from my server
ssh username@server
"rm my_remote_database.db.txt.gz"
# Uncompress the text file
gunzip
my_local_database.db.txt.gz
# Reconstruct the database from the text file
cat
my_local_database.db.txt | sqlite3 my_local_database.db
# Remove the local text file
rm
my_local_database.db.txt
A database dump is a stable copy source
This approach fixes another issue I’ve had when copying SQLite databases.
If it takes a long time to copy a database and it gets updated midway through, rsync may give me an invalid database file. The first half of the file is pre-update, the second half file is post-update, and they don’t match. When I try to open the database locally, I get an error:
database disk image is malformed
By creating a text dump before I start the copy operation, I’m giving rsync a stable copy source. That text dump isn’t going to change midway through the copy, so I’ll always get a complete and consistent text file.
This approach has saved me hours when working with large databases, and made my downloads both faster and more reliable. If you have to copy around large SQLite databases, give it a try.
43856186.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种更快速在计算机间复制大型SQLite数据库的方法。随着数据库增长，直接使用`rsync`复制变得缓慢且不可靠。作者发现索引导致数据库文件变大，复制效率低。通过使用SQLite的`.dump`命令，将数据库导出为文本文件，可以显著缩小文件体积，因为索引被转化为创建指令而非实际数据。导出的文本文件还可以通过gzip压缩，进一步减小体积。新的复制流程包括在服务器上创建gzip压缩的文本文件，然后使用`rsync`复制到本地，最后解压并重建数据库。此方法不仅加快了复制速度，还确保了数据库的一致性，避免了复制过程中数据库被更新导致的文件损坏问题。

主要讨论点：SQLite数据库备份与同步的方法及其效率优化

不同观点：
• **使用VACUUM INTO进行备份**：M95D认为使用`VACUUM INTO`命令备份SQLite数据库是高效的，可以减少文件系统I/O，并且备份文件体积最小化。
• **rsync的问题**：bambax指出直接使用rsync复制正在更新的数据库会导致文件损坏，因为更新过程中复制会导致文件前后不一致。他推荐使用Litestream来安全地复制SQLite数据库。
• **SQL语句传输与数据库传输的对比**：zeroq认为通过发送SQL语句来重建数据库并不一定比直接传输数据库更快，因为执行SQL语句还需要额外的时间和优化步骤（如执行/optimize/和/vacuum/）。
• **sqlite_rsync工具的优势**：hundredwatt提到新发布的sqlite_rsync工具使用优化的rsync算法来比较SQLite数据库的内部数据页，从而只同步更改或缺失的页，提高效率。
• **使用压缩**：mromanuk建议使用rsync的压缩功能（如-z和--compress-level）来加快传输速度，并指出压缩传输可以进一步优化。

data.title: Republicans want to tax EV drivers $200/year in new transport bill
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 美国众议院交通与基础设施委员会将讨论预算立法，拟对电动和混合动力汽车征收新年度费用。根据该提案，纯电动汽车需支付200美元年费，混合动力车支付100美元，而柴油车等高污染车辆仅需支付20美元，且2030年前无需缴费。该费用将随通胀逐年增加，直至2034年或2035年到期。尽管该税收预计在2035年前为公路信托基金增加1100亿美元收入，但整体资金仍短缺2220亿美元。批评者认为，该提案不公平地惩罚了环保车辆，并可能抑制电动汽车的普及。同时，商业车辆和农用车辆可豁免此费用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国是否正在陷入“资源诅咒”以及对电动汽车（EV）征税的合理性

不同观点：
• **[aurareturn的观点]**：美国成为世界第一大石油生产国可能会导致政治政策倾向于减缓电动汽车和混合动力车的普及，鼓励油价上涨，并忽视全球变暖问题。这与“资源诅咒”的理论相符，即丰富的自然资源可能导致经济和政治问题。

• **[carlhjerpe的观点]**：对电动汽车征收200美元年费的提议可能只是个人对特定人物（如Elon Musk）的不满，而不是基于实际经济影响。他认为这个金额对新车主来说影响不大。

• **[0xEF的观点]**：对新增税收应进行理性分析。他提出两个问题：1. 新增税收将用于什么项目？例如，修建更好的道路、充电站或改善交通基础设施？2. 如果这些资金用于有价值的项目，那么每年250美元是否真的太多？他指出，拥有电动汽车可以在汽油上节省大量费用，因此200美元的费用并不能有效阻止人们购买电动汽车。他还质疑该费用是否会被逐步提高到2000美元每年。

补充讨论：
• **[dlachausse的观点]**：没有直接发表意见，而是提供了先前讨论的链接，暗示对该话题已有较多讨论，可能认为当前讨论缺乏新意或需要参考之前的分析。

争议焦点：
• 美国作为石油生产大国，其政策是否会倾向于保护石油产业而抑制电动汽车的发展。
• 对电动汽车征收年费的合理性及其实际影响，特别是该费用是否会成为购买电动汽车的障碍。

WASHINGTON, DC—The House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee will meet today to discuss its proposed budget legislation, and there's a doozy in there for drivers of electric vehicles and hybrids. As part of the Republican Party's ongoing war against
science
and
the environment
under President Trump, committee chairperson Sam Graves (R-Mo.) has included some new annual fees that will cost all drivers some, but some drivers more.
Republicans plan to use the
budget reconciliation process
to pass this legislation, which is an expedited process that removes some of the US Senate's ability to stall. They're proposing a new annual federal motor vehicle registration fee, which state DMVs would have to collect and pass back to the federal government.
If it passes, all battery EVs would be subject to a new $200 tax. Hybrids—defined as vehicles that are propelled by both an electric motor and an internal combustion engine or other power source (which would include fuel cell EVs)—will pay $100. But someone who commutes 90 miles a day in a particulate-belching Ford F-350 Duramax diesel pickup truck gets away with a mere $20 a year, and only from October 1, 2030; until then they get to drive for free.
To make things even better, the bill requires these fees to be linked to inflation and should be increased each year, until 2034 when the tax expires for unelectrified vehicles, or 2035, the last year that EVs and hybrids would be taxed like this. So, a $200 registration fee in 2026 becomes a $250 registration fee in 2035.
Not everyone will have to pay, however. The bill exempts commercial vehicles, which should see a rush from tax avoiders to register their vehicles under their businesses, similar to what we saw during the George W. Bush administration, when a change in the tax law meant businesses
could claim a $100,000 tax credit
if they purchased a truck or SUV that weighed more than 6,000 lbs. Farm vehicles are also exempt from the law.
With EV adoption as low as it is in the US, the sums raised by these EV and hybrid charges will be essentially a rounding error in the federal budget, which this year should top $7 trillion. The Eno Center for Transportation calculates that this new tax will contribute an extra $110 billion to the highway Trust Fund by 2035 but that cuts to other taxes and more spending mean that the fund will still be $222 billion short of its commitments—assuming that this added fee doesn't further dampen EV adoption in the US, that is.
The committee cannot mandate that states collect these new taxes on drivers. But just as the federal government used the withholding of federal highway funds as a stick to force all states to raise the drinking age to 21, this bill would require the Department of Transportation to withhold 125 percent of the estimated total registration fees if it did not comply.
Graves' justification for this regressive attack on clean energy policies is that it's merely a matter of fairness, with a healthy side helping of the usual grievance politics. "Our proposal more than offsets these historic investments and reduces the deficit with rescissions of wasteful Green New Deal style spending from the Inflation Reduction Act and ensuring that electric vehicles begin paying their share for their use of the nation’s highways. It’s only fair that EVs pay these user fees like other motorists. In fact, the new user fees provision addresses the broken Highway Trust Fund revenue stream in a substantial manner for the first time in over 30 years," Graves said in a statement.
Making this move even more regressive, Graves notes in his statement that the vast majority of US states—39 in total—already charge
EV drivers a registration fee
, and 28 do the same for hybrid drivers. Graves also hints at the end of a federal gasoline tax, despite
ever-increasing levels of atmospheric CO
2
and the unequivocal evidence that this is caused by fossil fuel emissions.
"House Republicans are threatening to take away billions of dollars in funding that will help to slash health-threatening pollution, improve walkability, and rebuild communities harmed by highways," said Katherine Garcia, director of Sierra Club Clean Transportation for All.
"They're also trying to punish EV and hybrid drivers with an excessive annual fee rather than fixing the unsustainable Highway Trust Fund. Now is the time to incentivize, not penalize, people to drive cleaner vehicles that curb pollution harmful to our health and climate. Rather than spreading misinformation and attacking popular programs, Congress must focus on ensuring more Americans have access to clean transportation options. This proposal to shift critical funding and impose a punitive fee on Americans to pay for billionaire tax cuts is unacceptable."
Jonathan M. Gitlin
Automotive Editor
Jonathan M. Gitlin

data.title: ArkFlow: High-performance Rust stream processing engine
data.author: klaussilveira
data.article_summary: ArkFlow是一个高性能的Rust流处理引擎，具备强大的数据流处理能力，支持多种输入/输出源和处理器。主要特性包括：高性能（基于Rust和Tokio异步运行时）、支持多种数据源（如Kafka、MQTT、HTTP、文件等）、强大的处理能力（内置SQL查询、JSON处理、Protobuf编码/解码、批处理等）、可扩展的模块化设计。用户可以通过YAML配置文件定义日志级别、输入源、处理管道、输出目标和错误输出等。ArkFlow还提供了内存缓冲机制以处理背压和消息临时存储。示例包括从Kafka读取数据并处理后输出到Kafka，以及生成测试数据并进行处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ArkFlow项目的定位、技术特点及未来发展

不同观点：
• [chenquan] 认为ArkFlow是一个轻量级的分布式流处理引擎，旨在通过整合数据融合（datafusion）的大型生态系统和ArkFlow的可扩展能力，帮助社区简化数据处理的门槛，并创造更大的数据处理生态系统。他强调了流数据可以产生更大价值的核心信念，并对项目的未来充满信心。

• [coreyoconnor] 关注流处理的推广和教育问题，指出虽然流处理系统（如背压、断路器等概念）对于构建有弹性的系统至关重要，但在工程团队中推广流处理技术面临困难，团队往往更倾向于使用简单的同步程序，尽管这些程序通常更慢且更容易出错。

• [shawabawa3] 认为ArkFlow类似于https://vector.dev，但区别在于ArkFlow将数据转换为Apache Arrow格式并使用SQL查询，而vector.dev使用DSL（VRL）进行数据处理。

• [disintegrator] 和 [muffa] 都提到ArkFlow与Redpanda Connect (Benthos)非常相似，并关心ArkFlow的错误处理机制和消息传递保证。

• [gue-ni] 对"高性能"这一描述持怀疑态度，认为如果没有基准测试或与其他类似软件的性能对比，"高性能"只是一个无意义的 buzzword。

• [habobobo] 询问ArkFlow与arroyo和vector.dev的比较。

43833310.article_summary: ArkFlow是一个高性能的Rust流处理引擎，具备强大的数据流处理能力，支持多种输入/输出源和处理器。主要特性包括：高性能（基于Rust和Tokio异步运行时）、支持多种数据源（如Kafka、MQTT、HTTP、文件等）、强大的处理能力（内置SQL查询、JSON处理、Protobuf编码/解码、批处理等）、可扩展的模块化设计。用户可以通过YAML配置文件定义日志级别、输入源、处理管道、输出目标和错误输出等。ArkFlow还提供了内存缓冲机制以处理背压和消息临时存储。示例包括从Kafka读取数据并处理后输出到Kafka，以及生成测试数据并进行处理。

data.author: E-Reverance
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了一种在入门物理课程中不常见的观点：将物理视为**优化问题**。传统方法包括通过解析工具找到运动方程（分析法）或使用数值积分解决复杂系统（数值法）。然而，本文提出了一种不同的方法：**通过最小化作用量（action minimization）来求解物理系统的运动路径**。

具体来说，文章讨论了**拉格朗日方法**，该方法考虑系统从初始状态到最终状态的所有可能路径，并通过最小化作用量来选择实际路径。作用量 \(S\) 定义为拉格朗日量 \(L\)（动能减去势能）在时间上的积分。传统上，利用欧拉-拉格朗日方程可以求解系统的运动方程，而本文则尝试使用梯度下降法直接最小化作用量，以找到系统实际运动的路径。

文章最后通过一个自由落体问题演示了这一方法，并提到该方法适用于各种物理系统，包括经典力学、电磁学、热力学和相对论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于不同技术方法和理论的讨论，包括神经网络优化、物理模拟中的数学表示、以及确定性与混沌系统的理解。

不同观点：
• [gwern] 对小型神经网络（NN）的潜力表示赞赏，特别是其快速训练的能力，并分享了一篇展示相关技巧的文章链接。
• [jpfr] 将讨论与《SICM》这本书联系起来，指出文章中的路径表示为多项式，并提到未在库接口暴露底层优化方法，同时提供了相关章节的链接。
• [imtringued] 批评文章写作马虎，指出其在积分离散化和变量替换方面的不严谨，并提出了正确的数学表示方式，强调了文章在重要方程处理上的不足。
• [coderenegade] 分享了自己过去使用Hooke定律和有限元法进行类似研究的经验，并表示优化问题比ODE求解器更直观，同时对文章表示赞赏。
• [danbmil99] 针对 deterministic 系统提出异议，使用停机问题作为反例，暗示不能在不计算中间状态的情况下预知未来状态。
• [constantcrying] 强烈反对[danbmil99]的观点，强调确定性系统的特性，并解释了混沌系统的复杂性和数值求解器的误差增长问题，认为在某些情况下，即使不计算中间状态也能预知未来状态。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点集中在确定性系统和混沌系统的理解上，特别是在能否不通过中间状态直接预知未来状态的问题上存在分歧。
• [imtringued] 提供了具体的数学修正建议和链接，显示出对文章技术内容的深入分析和批评。
• [coderenegade] 的经验分享提供了一个实际应用的视角，强调了优化问题在实际工程中的价值。
• [danbmil99] 和 [constantcrying] 之间的争论反映了在理论计算机科学和物理模拟之间的跨学科理解差异。

Play
The purpose of this simple post is to bring to attention a view of physics which isn’t often communicated in introductory courses: the view of
physics as optimization
.
This approach begins with a quantity called the action. If you minimize the action, you can obtain a
path of least action
which represents the path a physical system will take through space and time. Generally speaking, physicists use analytic tools to do this minimization. In this post, we are going to attempt something different and slightly crazy: minimizing the action with gradient descent.
Read the paper
Run
in browser
Get the code
In this post.
In order to communicate this technique as clearly and concretely as possible, we’re going to apply it to a simple toy problem: a free body in a gravitational field. Keep in mind, though, that it works just as well on larger and more complex systems such as an ideal gas – we will treat these sorts of systems in the paper and in future blog posts.
Now, to put our approach in the proper context, we’re going to quickly review the standard approaches to this kind of problem.
Standard approaches
The analytical approach.
Here you use algebra, calculus, and other mathematical tools to find a closed-form equation of motion for the system. It gives the state of the system as a function of time. For an object in free fall, the equation of motion would be:
\[y(t)=-\frac{1}{2}gt^2+v_0t+y_0.\]

Not all physics problems have an analytical solution. Some, like the

or the
three-body problem
, are deterministic but chaotic. In other words, their dynamics are predictable but we can’t know their state at some time in the future without simulating all the intervening states. These we can solve with numerical integration. For the body in a gravitational field, here’s what the numerical approach would look like:

Our approach: action minimization
The Lagrangian method.
The approaches we just covered make intuitive sense. That’s why we teach them in introductory physics classes. But there is an entirely different way of looking at dynamics called the Lagrangian method. The Lagrangian method does a better job of describing reality because it can produce equations of motion for
any
physical system.
1
Lagrangians figure prominently in all four branches of physics: classical mechanics, electricity and magnetism, thermodynamics, and quantum mechanics. Without the Lagrangian method, physicists would have a hard time unifying these disparate fields. But with the
Standard Model Lagrangian
they can do precisely that.
How it works.
The Lagrangian method begins by considering all the paths a physical system could take from an initial state \(\bf{x}\)\((t_0)\) to a final state \(\bf{x}\)\((t_1)\). Then it provides a simple rule for selecting the path \(\hat{\bf x}\) that nature will actually take: the action \(S\), defined in the equation below, must have a stationary value over this path. Here \(T\) and \(V\) are the kinetic and potential energy functions for the system at any given time \(t\) in \([t_0,t_1]\).
\[\begin{aligned}
S &:= \int_{t_0}^{t_1} L({\bf x}, ~ \dot{\bf x}, ~ t) ~ dt\\
&\quad \textrm{where}\quad L = T - V \\
\quad \hat{\bf x} &~~ \textrm{has property}~ \frac{d}{dt} \left( \frac{\partial L}{\partial \dot{\hat{x}}(t)} \right) = \frac{\partial L}{\partial \hat{x}(t)} \\
&\textrm{for} \quad t \in [t_0,t_1]
\end{aligned}\]
Finding \(\hat{\bf x}\) with Euler-Lagrange (what people usually do).
When \(S\) is stationary, we can show that the Euler-Lagrange equation (third line in the equation above) holds true over the interval \([t_0,t_1]\) (Morin, 2008). This observation is valuable because it allows us to solve for \(\hat{\bf x}\): first we apply the Euler-Lagrange equation to the Lagrangian \(L\) and derive a system of partial differential equations.
2
Then we integrate those equations to obtain \(\hat{\bf x}\). Importantly, this approach works for all problems spanning classical mechanics, electrodynamics, thermodynamics, and relativity. It provides a coherent theoretical framework for studying classical physics as a whole.

data.title: Are you the same person you used to be? (2022)
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了人们对幼年记忆的模糊性以及自我身份随时间变化的问题。作者作为四岁孩子的父亲，与儿子共度欢乐时光，但疑惑儿子将来能记住多少现在的生活。作者自己对四岁时的记忆零散，难以拼凑出完整的自我。文章进一步讨论了人们是否在四岁、二十四岁、四十四岁或七十四岁时仍是同一个人，还是发生了根本变化。有些人感到与过去的自己有强烈联系，而另一些人则感觉像完全不同的人。文中引用了Wordsworth的诗句，指出童年与成年可能存在联系，但也可能只是错觉。有些人希望与过去的自我分离，甚至建议用不同名字代表人生不同阶段，以反映每个阶段的独特性和连续性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人成长与自我认知的变化，以及如何看待过去的自己与现在的自己之间的关系。

不同观点：
• [bluefirebrand] 认为成功来自于专注于“我想成为什么样的人”，而非纠结于“我是谁”。他强调通过妥协和努力实现了自己想要的生活，并认为过度关注身份问题可能带来负面影响。他以自己的成功为例，表明这种方法的有效性。
• [jawns] 引用了《Mysterious Benedict Society》一书，提出人们在成长过程中不仅仅是变成不同的人，而是“积累”了更多的自己。他认为每个人的过去与现在共同塑造了现在的自己，并以长期的婚姻关系为例说明这种观点。
• [frankus] 引用了Hank Green的演讲，主张不必对过去的梦想负责，过去 self 的梦想不应束缚现在的自己。
• [ainiriand] 表达了对失去童年无条件幸福感的怀念，并指出成年后的幸福感变得复杂，受多种因素影响。
• [GuardianCaveman] 引用了Emerson的名言，强调经历和体验对塑造个人精神的重要性，而非仅仅记住具体的经历。
• [codr7] 以幽默的方式表示自己比以往更接近记住“我是谁”。
• [behnamoh] 讨论了真实记忆与合成记忆的区别，并担忧数字时代的记忆保存问题。他还对“自我”的概念提出哲学性疑问。
• [MarkusWandel] 强调了生活经验对改变自我身体和心灵的影响，认为这是一个连续变化的过程。
• [xyzelement] 认为个人的成长是家庭核心价值观的自然体现，并以自身从工程师到父亲和领导者的角色转变为例，说明自我进化是适应环境和价值观追求的结果。
• [moomin] 直言不讳地表示自己与童年时完全不同，并对过去的自己有复杂的感受。
• [wdrw] 提出通过刻意努力可以恢复更多童年记忆，并分享了自己的记忆恢复方法。
• [throwanem] 认为自己不应与过去的孩子相同，因为现在拥有过去没有的知识和经验。
• [stronglikedan] 表示自己虽然是过去自己的产物，但并不与过去相同。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一在于“自我认知”与“身份认同”的问题，一些人如[bluefirebrand]认为过度关注“我是谁”可能带来负面影响，而[jawns]等人则认为过去的自己与现在的自己共同构成了完整的自我。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对童年记忆的看法，[wdrw]认为通过努力可以恢复更多记忆，而[behnamoh]则对记忆的真实性提出质疑。
• 成长与自我进化是贯穿评论的核心主题，不同评论者从个人经历、哲学思考和具体方法等角度分享了各自的见解。

I have few memories of being four—a fact I find disconcerting now that I’m the father of a four-year-old. My son and I have great times together; lately, we’ve been building Lego versions of familiar places (the coffee shop, the bathroom) and perfecting the “flipperoo,” a move in which I hold his hands while he somersaults backward from my shoulders to the ground. But how much of our joyous life will he remember? What I recall from when I was four are the red-painted nails of a mean babysitter; the brushed-silver stereo in my parents’ apartment; a particular orange-carpeted hallway; some houseplants in the sun; and a glimpse of my father’s face, perhaps smuggled into memory from a photograph. These disconnected images don’t knit together into a picture of a life. They also fail to illuminate any inner reality. I have no memories of my own feelings, thoughts, or personality; I’m told that I was a cheerful, talkative child given to long dinner-table speeches, but don’t remember being so. My son, who is happy and voluble, is so much fun to be around that I sometimes mourn, on his behalf, his future inability to remember himself.
If we could see our childish selves more clearly, we might have a better sense of the course and the character of our lives. Are we the same people at four that we will be at twenty-four, forty-four, or seventy-four? Or will we change substantially through time? Is the fix already in, or will our stories have surprising twists and turns? Some people feel that they’ve altered profoundly through the years, and to them the past seems like a foreign country, characterized by peculiar customs, values, and tastes. (Those boyfriends! That music! Those outfits!) But others have a strong sense of connection with their younger selves, and for them the past remains a home. My mother-in-law, who lives not far from her parents’ house in the same town where she grew up, insists that she is the same as she’s always been, and recalls with fresh indignation her sixth birthday, when she was promised a pony but didn’t get one. Her brother holds the opposite view: he looks back on several distinct epochs in his life, each with its own set of attitudes, circumstances, and friends. “I’ve walked through many doorways,” he’s told me. I feel this way, too, although most people who know me well say that I’ve been the same person forever.
Try to remember life as you lived it years ago, on a typical day in the fall. Back then, you cared deeply about certain things (a girlfriend? Depeche Mode?) but were oblivious of others (your political commitments? your children?). Certain key events—college? war? marriage? Alcoholics Anonymous?—hadn’t yet occurred. Does the self you remember feel like you, or like a stranger? Do you seem to be remembering yesterday, or reading a novel about a fictional character?
If you have the former feelings, you’re probably a continuer; if the latter, you’re probably a divider. You might prefer being one to the other, but find it hard to shift your perspective. In the poem “The Rainbow,” William Wordsworth wrote that “the Child is Father of the Man,” and this motto is often quoted as truth. But he couched the idea as an aspiration—“And I could wish my days to be / Bound each to each by natural piety”—as if to say that, though it would be nice if our childhoods and adulthoods were connected like the ends of a rainbow, the connection could be an illusion that depends on where we stand. One reason to go to a high-school reunion is to feel like one’s past self—old friendships resume, old in-jokes resurface, old crushes reignite. But the time travel ceases when you step out of the gym. It turns out that you’ve changed, after all.
On the other hand, some of us want to disconnect from our past selves; burdened by who we used to be or caged by who we are, we wish for multipart lives. In the voluminous autobiographical novel “My Struggle,” Karl Ove Knausgaard—a middle-aged man who hopes to be better today than he was as a young man—questions whether it even makes sense to use the same name over a lifetime. Looking at a photograph of himself as an infant, he wonders what that little person, with “arms and legs spread, and a face distorted into a scream,” really has to do with the forty-year-old father and writer he is now, or with “the gray, hunched geriatric who in forty years from now might be sitting dribbling and trembling in an old people’s home.” It might be better, he suggests, to adopt a series of names: “The fetus might be called Jens Ove, for example, and the infant Nils Ove . . . the ten- to twelve-year-old Geir Ove, the twelve- to seventeen-year-old Kurt Ove . . . the twenty-three- to thirty-two-year-old Tor Ove, the thirty-two- to forty-six-year-old Karl Ove—and so on.” In such a scheme, “the first name would represent the distinctiveness of the age range, the middle name would represent continuity, and the last, family aff

data.title: Judge rules Apple executive lied under oath, makes criminal contempt referral
data.author: connor11528
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果公司股票价格波动及其背后的原因，涉及法律问题、公司高层管理、财务影响等多方面。

不同观点：
• Imustaskforhelp 认为苹果的股票价格在盘后交易中下跌了2.3%，并通过计算得出苹果市值损失了890亿美元。他对此表示担忧，认为这一波动可能反映了市场对苹果失去信心。
• rdtsc 和 yalogin 等人关注法院文件中的证词，特别是苹果高管Roman的证词，认为其存在误导和不实陈述，可能对公司造成负面影响。
• kace91 和 post_break 批评苹果高层管理，特别是Tim Cook的决策，认为其在法律和道德上存在问题，可能需要进行领导层更替。
• Eddy_Viscosity2 和 dataflow 对高管是否会面临刑事指控表示怀疑，认为即使面临指控，也可能不会被定罪或被赦免。
• fencepost 关心开发者是否能通过法律途径追讨损失，质疑苹果是否会受到实际的经济处罚。
• AtlasBarfed 将讨论引向更广泛的政治背景，指出参议员Jim Jordan试图通过削弱反垄断法的行为。
• JumpCrisscross 提供John Gruber对裁决的总结，强调不同高管在处理法律裁决上的态度差异。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了苹果在法律和财务上的双重挑战，特别是与反垄断裁决相关的问题。
• 一些评论质疑苹果高管的诚信和管理能力，特别是对公司在法律纠纷中的应对策略表示不满。
• 有评论指出这一股票价格波动可能与即将公布的财报有关，暗示市场对公司未来表现的担忧。

争议焦点：
• 苹果高管是否在证词中存在故意误导和不实陈述。
• 苹果是否会在法律裁决中面临实际的经济和刑事处罚。
• 市场对苹果股票价格波动的反应是否过度，或者是否反映了更深层次的公司问题。

data.title: Vanguard 50-year anniversary CEO letter
data.author: telotortium
data.article_summary: Vanguard CEO Salim Ramji在2025年5月发布了一封致投资者的公开信，庆祝公司成立50周年。自1975年由Jack Bogle创立以来，Vanguard一直致力于为投资者提供低成本、高可及性的投资服务，公司由投资者所有，旨在为他们创造收益，而非从他们身上获利。Vanguard通过降低指数基金和主动管理基金的成本，帮助投资者保留更多回报，并已多次削减费用。公司还将这一“Vanguard效应”扩展至固定收益和现金储蓄领域，特别是在市场波动时强调多元化投资的重要性。Vanguard承诺将继续专注于长期投资成功，并感谢投资者一直以来的信任。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Vanguard及指数基金投资的多种观点和讨论，包括其历史影响、未来可持续性、技术问题、费用结构、以及道德和阴谋论等相关问题。

不同观点：
• 支持Vanguard及指数基金：
  - shartshooter分享了个人经历，表示受祖父母影响，长期投资Vanguard 500指数基金，最终受益匪浅，强调了定期投资（dollar cost averaging）的优势。
  - jjice高度赞扬Vanguard创始人Jack Bogle，认为他对普通投资者做出了巨大贡献，通过降低费用和推广被动投资改变了行业生态。
  - d_burfoot表示喜欢Vanguard的运营模式，尤其是其高层并非超级富豪，认为这种模式对大众有益。

• 对指数基金未来的担忧：
  - bix6提出疑问，指数基金未来是否仍能作为普通人的金融救星，担心少数大公司掌握过多权力，可能导致潜在风险。
  - RivieraKid提到指数基金ETF可能面临的隐性费用问题，例如因股票回购或股权增加导致的年度费用接近1%。

• 对Vanguard技术及服务的不满：
  - bklyn11201抱怨Vanguard的客户端 web界面不如竞争对手，希望了解其技术挑战或是否有意为之。
  - nknealk指出Vanguard在2025年大幅削减费用，显示其在费用结构上的持续创新。

• 对指数基金的道德与阴谋论质疑：
  - fancymcpoopoo将指数基金比作不道德的金字塔骗局，认为鼓励所有人投资于大公司是盲目追求利润。
  - martinky24认为讨论中很多是Vanguard的营销宣传。
  - alecco批评支持指数基金的人吹嘘泡沫，暗示其对价值投资的破坏。
  - bearcobra担心网上对Vanguard等公司的误解和阴谋论，认为这对ETF的未来构成风险。

• 对环境和社会责任的关注：
  - ijustlovemath希望Vanguard推出零化石燃料基金，表达了对环保投资产品的需求。

补充讨论：
- solatic强烈反对对指数基金的负面看法，认为投资美国股市指数基金是通过利用美国企业CEO的贪婪来获利，且这种力量不可阻挡。
- 整体讨论反映了不同投资者对费用、技术、未来风险及道德问题的关注，以及对Vanguard和指数基金模式的多角度审视。

My fellow Vanguard investor,
Fifty years ago today, Jack Bogle started a different kind of investment firm—one owned by its investors, ensuring a focus on making money for them, not from them.
1
Hear from our founder what makes Vanguard different
Read the transcript
John C. Bogle:
What made Vanguard different from everybody else in this industry was the structure that I picked in the first place, way back in 1974. We are owned by the shareholders. Our mission is to serve them and not some outside management company owner.
And I don't think it's self-serving to say that we are a company that is of the shareholder, by the shareholder, and for the shareholder, with a crew that understands that and implements it really quite beautifully.
People are the key to everything we do and everything we ever have done. I've often talked about human beings being the hallmark of this operation—people that care about our values, people that care about our integrity, each with their own hopes and fears and financial goals.
Read more
Vanguard was founded on the ideal that all investors deserve a fair shake—that investing ought to be lower-cost and more accessible. Bogle’s idealism was audacious at the time. data.article_summary: Linkwarden 2.9是一款多功能网页和文档保存工具，支持用户在一个平台上收集、组织和共享网页链接及文档。它具备自动保存网页内容、防止链接失效的功能，并允许团队协作和权限设置。该工具提供开源和自托管选项，支持暗/亮模式切换、批量操作、导入导出等功能，并有浏览器扩展便于使用。用户可选择云端或自定义方案，享受14天免费试用。数千用户对其书签管理和内容存档功能给予高度评价。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linkwarden及其类似工具的功能、性能、使用场景和竞争产品对比

不同观点：
• Daniel31x13（开发者）介绍了Linkwarden的核心功能，包括文本高亮、全页存档、全内容搜索、AI标签、浏览器同步和协作功能，并指出自托管用户也能使用云计划中的所有功能。
• Virtualcharles对比了Raindrop和自托管选项（如Hoarder），表示自己倾向于付费让别人处理服务，但也在考虑自托管选项。
• Evanjrowley分享了使用Karakeep（前Hoarder）的经验，指出其正在开发Safari扩展，同时提到Linkwarden缺乏Safari支持，并讨论了浏览器资源消耗问题。
• Dennisy质疑保存网页链接的实际用途，询问人们如何使用这些保存的链接。
• Gibibit关注网站存档的可信度和验证问题，建议使用区块链技术，但指出技术上仍有缺失。
• Manmal赞扬了Linkwarden的速度和稳定性，提到在Hetzner VPS上运行良好，但初期从Pinboard导入时遇到内存问题。
• Raybb希望增加离线支持，以满足在网络不稳定情况下的使用需求。
• Carterschonwald询问是否可以导入Pinboard或类似数据。
• Aiono将Linkwarden与Readeck对比，认为前者可能更“重量级”。
• Spyder提到了KaraKeep，并提供了其GitHub链接。
• Ibaikov分享了自托管Linkwarden的经验，指出其比Karakeep/Hoarder更轻量，但仍希望增加拖放链接保存功能和优化资源使用。
• Mikae1提供了多个类似工具的链接，如Linkace、Linkding、Espial、Postmarks、Mycorrhiza Wiki和Linkhut。
• Xwat提到Linkwarden在导入书签时会创建重复项，并提供了相关GitHub问题链接。
• FireInsight表示希望从Linkding升级到Linkwarden，期待其同步书签和文章高亮功能。
• Nickfixit表示喜欢Hoarder（KaraKeep），提到其具有API和MCP服务器，并表示会尝试Linkwarden。

补充讨论：
• 关于浏览器扩展的支持，特别是Safari扩展的缺乏，是部分用户关注的问题。
• 自托管与付费服务的选择是另一个讨论焦点，部分用户倾向于付费服务以减少自托管的麻烦。
• 资源消耗问题在多个评论中被提及，尤其是与类似工具（如Karakeep/Hoarder）的对比。
• 用户对可信存档和验证功能的技术实现（如区块链应用）表示关注，但对其现状不太满意。
• 导入数据（特别是从Pinboard）和书签重复问题是技术细节上的重要讨论点。

data.title: Trust Me, I'm Local: Chrome Extensions, MCP, and the Sandbox Escape
data.author: el_duderino
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Chrome扩展程序与本地MCP（Model Context Protocol）服务器交互所带来的严重安全风险。MCP服务器通常缺乏身份验证机制，导致任何Chrome扩展可以在无需特殊权限的情况下访问本地资源，甚至可能完全接管机器。文章描述了一个实例：一个Chrome扩展与本地MCP服务器通信，未经认证即可操作文件系统等敏感资源。由于Chrome的沙箱模型无法阻止这种攻击，用户面临极大的安全威胁。文章呼吁开发者和用户重新评估本地MCP服务器的安全性，以防止潜在的灾难性后果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Chrome扩展和MCP（或本地服务器）之间的安全问题，特别是与本地主机连接相关的风险和解决方案。

不同观点：
• **telotortium**：认为问题与MCP无关，而是Chrome扩展可以连接到本地主机端口，任何服务器都可以。这并不是一个无限制的后门，Chrome扩展已经需要权限才能与localhost通信。
• **fluffet**：对互联网协议和AI工具的演变感到担忧，认为历史教训（如加密和监管的重要性）正在被遗忘，AI技术可能重蹈覆辙。
• **npace12**：分享了自己创建的Chrome扩展“little-rat”，可以跟踪和阻止其他扩展的流量，提供了一种实际解决方案。
• **skybrian**：指出“允许连接到localhost”的权限听起来无害，但随着本地端口上运行的服务器增多，风险增加。用户需要了解所有本地进程的工作原理，但大多数人并不了解。
• **bhelx**：首次听说使用SSE传输本地数据，建议将MCP服务器运行在沙盒环境中，并使用Wasm技术以增强安全性。
• **OsrsNeedsf2P**：质疑MCP是否因为没有安全摩擦而击败了其他竞争对手，暗示安全性和用户体验之间的平衡。
• **happyopossum**：认为这不是MCP的问题，任何监听localhost的应用都可能被扩展攻击，MCP并没有使问题变得更容易或更糟。
• **fpoling**：建议拒绝带有Origin头和UserAgent的HTTP请求，以增强安全性。
• **babyshake**：询问是否可以通过使用streamable HTTP MCP服务器来避免此漏洞，并讨论了不同传输方法的优缺点。
• **olalonde**：提出是通过为MCP服务器添加身份验证，还是通过Chrome限制未经授权的localhost调用来解决问题。
• **brap**：质疑为什么需要一个新的协议（MCP），认为已有像OpenAPI这样的工具可以实现类似功能，并支持本地使用。
• **_pdp_**：指出MCP配置中明文存储凭据的问题，认为这是安全上的倒退。
• **rvz**：预测使用MCP服务器的初创公司将来可能面临安全事件，并为此付出高昂的代价。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于MCP是否引入了新的安全问题，还是这些问题在其他情况下（如普通web服务器）也同样存在。
• 讨论中多次提到身份验证和权限控制作为可能的解决方案，但也有人质疑这些措施的实际可行性和必要性。
• 对新协议（MCP）的需求和其相对于现有工具（如OpenAPI）的优势存在争议。
• 安全性与用户体验之间的平衡是一个反复出现的主题，尤其是在新技术（如AI工具和MCP）快速发展的背景下。

Featured
Trust Me, I’m Local: Chrome Extensions, MCP, and the Sandbox Escape
Yuval Ronen
Follow
6 min read
·
Apr 24, 2025
--
Listen
Share
Let’s talk about MCPs. You’ve probably heard of them, and maybe you’ve read the security risks associated with them. Sure, they sound worrying, but when you put them into a real-world context, they can quickly become far more concerning than you can ever imagine.
Just last week, our system flagged a suspicious Chrome extension. It sent messages to a port on localhost — nothing too odd at first glance, but as we dug deeper, we found that this extension communicated with an MCP server running on the local machine.
The fact that Chrome extensions can communicate with MCPs is a serious risk. The consequences are enormous. The usual security measures like Chrome’s sandbox model, don’t stand a chance.
You’re looking at unauthenticated access to the filesystem and, in some cases, a full machine takeover. That’s not just a small issue;
that’s a massive, game-changing vulnerability.
And here’s the kicker:
any
Chrome extension can exploit this. No special permissions required. If there’s a vulnerable MCP server running on a host machine, that’s it. We’ve already found vulnerable MCP servers tied to services like filesystem access, Slack, WhatsApp, and more. This isn’t just a theoretical risk anymore, it’s real, and the impact could be devastating.
So, if you’re running MCP locally, it’s time to seriously reevaluate your security. We were mindblown when we found this, and it’s time everyone else takes notice before it’s too late.
So, buckle up and get ready, let’s dive into this together.
A Suspicious localhost connection
While monitoring browser extension activity, our detection engine flagged a Chrome extension making network requests to localhost. Although the extension itself showed no signs of malicious behavior, the destination caught our attention. It was communicating with a local service implementing the
Model Context Protocol (MCP)
— a protocol used to interface AI agents with system tools and resources on the endpoint.
localhost MCP connection from chrome extension
This raised an immediate concern: if a browser extension can talk to an MCP server running on the user’s machine, what’s stopping it from accessing sensitive resources or executing privileged actions through the MCP?
MCP: Open by Default
Let’s first understand how MCP clients communicate with MCP servers. There are 2 standard transport implementations -
Server-Sent Events (SSE) — enables the MCP server to communicate through HTTP POST requests.
Standard Input/Output (stdio) — enables the MCP server to communicate through the process’s standard input and output streams.
When implementing an MCP server, the developer can choose how the MCP server will communicate. The server can support both transport methods.
It’s important to note that the transport layers themselves do not implement, or require, any authentication mechanism. It is up to the MCP server developer to implement access controls, but in practice, nearly all MCP servers today do not enforce authentication by default.
For local use, an MCP server that relies on Server-Sent Events (SSE) typically binds to a port on localhost, making it accessible from processes running on the same machine (like an MCP client).

Now that we understand how a local SSE-based MCP server operates, and that it’s generally accessible to processes running on the same machine, we can revisit the question: can a Chrome extension access it as well?
The communication flow is fairly straightforward:
The client sends a GET request to the server to obtain a session ID and a messages endpoint — without any form of authentication.
Once initialized, the client can issue POST requests to that message’s endpoint to retrieve the list of available tools exposed by the MCP server and invoke them directly.
Client-Server communication illustration
First we set up a local SSE-based MCP server from
mcp.so
, specifically choosing a file-system variant, which allows AI clients to interact with the local file system. Following the setup instructions in the server’s README:
node dist/index.js ~/work/mcp/private_directory
Next we built a Chrome extension that runs in the background and attempts to connect to localhost:3001 - a commonly used port for local SSE-based MCP servers. Of course, this port may vary, so a real-world extension would need to scan local ports to locate the active MCP instance. The extension gets the server information, retrieves the tools list and tries to invoke the tools provided by the MCP server:
The Chrome extension had
unrestricted
access to the MCP server’s tools — no authentication needed — and was interacting with the file system as if it were a core part of the server’s exposed capabilities. The potential impact of this is massive, opening the door for malicious exploitation and complete system compromise.

43856656.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Chrome扩展和MCP（或本地服务器）之间的安全问题，特别是与本地主机连接相关的风险和解决方案。

不同观点：
• **telotortium**：认为问题与MCP无关，而是Chrome扩展可以连接到本地主机端口，任何服务器都可以。这并不是一个无限制的后门，Chrome扩展已经需要权限才能与localhost通信。
• **fluffet**：对互联网协议和AI工具的演变感到担忧，认为历史教训（如加密和监管的重要性）正在被遗忘，AI技术可能重蹈覆辙。
• **npace12**：分享了自己创建的Chrome扩展“little-rat”，可以跟踪和阻止其他扩展的流量，提供了一种实际解决方案。
• **skybrian**：指出“允许连接到localhost”的权限听起来无害，但随着本地端口上运行的服务器增多，风险增加。用户需要了解所有本地进程的工作原理，但大多数人并不了解。
• **bhelx**：首次听说使用SSE传输本地数据，建议将MCP服务器运行在沙盒环境中，并使用Wasm技术以增强安全性。
• **OsrsNeedsf2P**：质疑MCP是否因为没有安全摩擦而击败了其他竞争对手，暗示安全性和用户体验之间的平衡。
• **happyopossum**：认为这不是MCP的问题，任何监听localhost的应用都可能被扩展攻击，MCP并没有使问题变得更容易或更糟。
• **fpoling**：建议拒绝带有Origin头和UserAgent的HTTP请求，以增强安全性。
• **babyshake**：询问是否可以通过使用streamable HTTP MCP服务器来避免此漏洞，并讨论了不同传输方法的优缺点。
• **olalonde**：提出是通过为MCP服务器添加身份验证，还是通过Chrome限制未经授权的localhost调用来解决问题。
• **brap**：质疑为什么需要一个新的协议（MCP），认为已有像OpenAPI这样的工具可以实现类似功能，并支持本地使用。
• **_pdp_**：指出MCP配置中明文存储凭据的问题，认为这是安全上的倒退。
• **rvz**：预测使用MCP服务器的初创公司将来可能面临安全事件，并为此付出高昂的代价。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于MCP是否引入了新的安全问题，还是这些问题在其他情况下（如普通web服务器）也同样存在。
• 讨论中多次提到身份验证和权限控制作为可能的解决方案，但也有人质疑这些措施的实际可行性和必要性。
• 对新协议（MCP）的需求和其相对于现有工具（如OpenAPI）的优势存在争议。
• 安全性与用户体验之间的平衡是一个反复出现的主题，尤其是在新技术（如AI工具和MCP）快速发展的背景下。

data.article_summary: Hyperparam是一家致力于解决机器学习中数据处理工具不足问题的公司，旨在提供一个用户友好、可扩展的界面，帮助数据科学家高效探索和处理大规模数据集。其核心目标是提升数据质量，因为数据质量对ML模型的成功至关重要。Hyperparam通过高效的数据格式、高性能JavaScript库以及AI辅助技术，使用户能够在浏览器中直接查看和处理TB级数据，而无需复杂的基础设施。其产品包括开源工具Hyparquet，一个纯JavaScript实现的Parquet文件读取库，支持在浏览器中无服务器访问大型数据集，具备高效流处理、压缩支持和轻量级特性。Hyperparam的愿景是通过数据质量的提升，促进更好模型的开发，同时确保隐私和合规性。

43857856.article_content:
Hyperparam Open-Source
Hyperparam was founded to address a critical gap in the machine learning ecosystem: the lack of a user-friendly, scalable UI for exploring and curating massive datasets.
Our mission is grounded in the belief that data quality is the most important factor in ML success, and that better tools are needed to build better training sets. In practice, this means enabling data scientists and engineers to
“look at your data”
– even terabyte-scale text corpora – interactively and entirely in-browser without heavy infrastructure. By combining efficient data formats, high-performance JavaScript libraries, and emerging AI assistance, Hyperparam's vision is to put data quality front and center in model development. Our motto
“the missing UI for AI data”
reflects its goal to make massive data exploration, labeling, and quality management as intuitive as modern web apps, all while respecting privacy and compliance through a local-first design.
Mission and Vision: Data-Centric AI in the Browser
Our mission is to empower ML practitioners to create the best training datasets for the best models. This stems from an industry-wide realization that
model performance is ultimately bounded by data quality
, not just model architecture or hyperparameters. Hyperparam envisions a new workflow where:
Interactive Data Exploration at Scale:
Users can freely explore huge datasets (millions or billions of records) with fast, free-form interactions to uncover insights. Unlike traditional Python notebooks that struggle with large data (often requiring downsampling or clunky pagination), Hyperparam leverages browser technology for a smooth UI.
AI-Assisted Curation:
Hyperparam integrates ML models to help label, filter, and transform data at a scale that would be impractical to review manually. By combining a highly interactive UI with model assistance, we make it possible for the user to use data to express exactly what they want from the model.
Local-First and Private:
Hyperparam runs entirely client-side, with no server dependency. This design not only simplifies setup (no complex pipeline or cloud needed) but also addresses enterprise compliance and security concerns, since sensitive data need not leave the user's machine. Fully browser-contained tools can bypass major adoption hurdles.
Experts across data engineering and MLOps widely agree on the need for better data exploration and labeling tools to tackle today's bottlenecks. We believe that the way to do that is to make data-centric AI workflows that are faster, easier to deploy, and more scalable – enabling users to iteratively improve data quality, which in turn yields better models.
The Hyperparam OSS Universe
Hyperparam delivers on our vision through a suite of open-source tools that tackle different aspects of data curation. These tools are built in TypeScript/JavaScript for seamless browser and Node.js usage.
We care about performance, minimal dependencies, and standards compliance.
Hyparquet: In-Browser Parquet Data Access
Hyparquet
is a lightweight, pure-JS library for reading
Apache Parquet
files directly in the browser. Parquet is a popular columnar format for large datasets, and Hyparquet enables web applications to tap into that efficiency without any server.
Hyparquet allows data scientists to open large dataset files instantly in a browser UI for examination, without needing Python scripts, servers, or cloud databases. It's useful for quick dataset validation (e.g. checking a sample of a new data for quality issues) and for powering web-based data analysis tools. Because it's pure JS, developers can integrate Hyparquet into any web app or Electron application that needs to read Parquet. It is the core engine behind Hyperparam's own dataset viewer, enabling what was previously thought impossible:
client-side
big data exploration.
Browser-Native & Dependency-Free:
Hyparquet has
zero external dependencies
and is designed to run in both modern browsers and Node.js. At ~9.7 KB gzipped, it's extremely lightweight. It implements the full Parquet specification, aiming to be the “world's most compliant Parquet parser” that can open more files (all encodings and types) than other libraries.
Efficient Streaming of Massive Data:
Built with performance in mind, Hyparquet only loads the portions of data needed for a given query or view. It leverages Parquet's built-in indexing to fetch just the required rows or columns on the fly. This “load just in time” approach makes it feasible to interactively explore multi-gigabyte or even billion-row datasets in a web app.
Complete Compression Support:
Parquet files often use compression (Snappy, Gzip, ZSTD, etc.). Hyparquet by default handles common cases (uncompressed, Snappy), and with a companion library Hyparquet-Compressors, it supports
all
Parquet compression codecs. This is achieved with WebAssembly-optimized decompressors – notably HySnappy, a WASM Snappy decoder that accelerates parsing with minimal footprint.

• [parpfish] 提出疑问，为什么劳动问题没有在科技工作者中引起更多共鸣。他认为，尽管科技工作者对工作不满有很多讨论，但当涉及到组织工会时，很多人却持鄙视态度，因为他们深受个人主义的"奋斗文化"影响，认为工会只是帮助懒惰的寄生虫。

• [stuaxo] 主张实行四天工作制，认为这是对当前工作制度的必要改革，类似于历史上从10-16小时工作日缩短到8小时的进步。

• [TimTheTinker] 讨论了马克思主义的起源及其在工业革命后工人运动中的影响力，同时指出布尔什维克革命的负面后果。他认为法治是解决不公的最佳途径，但当不公持续太久时，人们容易被意识形态煽动，导致社会的剧烈变动。

• [navigate8310] 提出关于“五一节”与航空紧急求救信号“Mayday”之间是否有联系的疑问。

• [graemep] 和 [OJFord] 指出“五一节”作为夏季节庆的起源远早于其作为劳工节日的含义，并强调了该节日在不同国家和文化中的多样性。

• [candiddevmike] 和 [PaulRobinson] 讨论了劳动运动的历史和现状，包括英国和美国的情况。他们指出劳动条件的改善以及近期出现的零时合同和 gig economy 对劳动权利的挑战，并提出是否会出现新的劳动运动或复兴旧运动的可能性。

• [0xbadcafebee] 反对二元对立的观点，主张在不同的社会结构和思想体系之间找到平衡，认为妥协和多样性是避免冲突的关键。

• [throw0101a] 解释了为什么美国选择九月份的劳动节而非五月一日的国际劳动节，指出这与避免与社会主义和无政府主义运动的关联有关。

补充讨论：
• [booleandilemma] 和 [soupfordummies] 表达了对国际劳动节假期的羡慕和对历史上工人斗争的感慨。
• [ramesh31] 简单表达了对劳动团结的支持。

争议的焦点：
• 劳动节及其历史意义的不同理解和解释。
• 工会和劳动运动在现代科技和经济环境下的相关性和有效性。
• 工作时间和工作条件的改革必要性及其可能的实现方式。
• 在社会结构和思想体系中是否应采取极端立场或寻找中间道路。

data.title: All roses were once yellow
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 一项大规模基因组分析显示，所有颜色的玫瑰，包括红色、粉色和白色，都源自一种黄色、单瓣、七小叶的共同祖先。北京林业大学的研究人员通过分析205个样本、84个玫瑰物种的基因组，揭示了玫瑰的进化和地理历史。研究表明，现代玫瑰起源于中国，并在驯化过程中发展出多种颜色和花型。面对气候变化，育种者正利用野生玫瑰的遗传资源，培育抗旱、抗病的品种。该研究为现代玫瑰的育种和濒危品种的保护提供了重要基础。相关成果发表在《Nature Plants》期刊上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：玫瑰的原始形态及其经过人类选择性培育后的变化

不同观点：
• [abeppu的观点] 认为我们对于某些生命形态的基本认知是被人类数百年来选择性培育所扭曲的版本。例如，原始的玫瑰通常只有单排花瓣，虽然这些品种 still 被栽培，但它们看起来并不像大多数人印象中的玫瑰。这与其他水果和蔬菜的野生祖先经过高度选择性培育后变得与现代品种大不相同类似。

• [kees99的观点] 对 abeppu 的说法提出质疑，认为根据“玫瑰属”（genus Rosa）的定义，abeppu 的说法可能是错误的。kees99 以野生的犬玫瑰（Rosa canina）为例，指出这种野玫瑰是粉红色的，并提供了维基百科的链接以支持其论点。

补充讨论：
• abeppu 强调了人类对自然生物的改造和选择性培育如何改变了我们对这些生物原始形态的认知。
• kees99 则通过具体的生物学定义和实例（犬玫瑰的颜色）来反驳 abeppu 的观点，指出并非所有野生玫瑰都符合 abeppu 所描述的单排花瓣特征。
• 争议的焦点在于玫瑰的原始形态及其现代变种之间的差异，特别是关于“玫瑰属”定义下的具体例子（如犬玫瑰）是否支持 abeppu 的论点。

Red, pink or white, all roses were once yellow says genomic analysis
by Sanjukta Mondal										 										 , Phys.org
The ancestor of roses could have had yellow, unspotted petals and leaves with seven leaflets. Credit: Anna Shvets: https://www.pexels.com/photo/person-holding-white-roses-bouquet-5894037/
Red roses, the symbol of love, were likely yellow in the past, indicates
a large genomic analysis
by researchers from Beijing Forestry University, China. Roses of all colors, including white, red, pink, and peach, belong to the genus Rosa, which is a member of the Rosaceae family.
Reconstructing the ancestral traits through genomic analysis revealed that all the roads trace back to a
common ancestor
—a single-petal flower with yellow color and seven leaflets.
The findings are published in
Nature Plants
.
Accounting for almost 30% of the cut flower market sales, roses are the most widely cultivated ornamental plants and have been successfully domesticated to reflect the aesthetic preferences of each era.
It all began with the rose breeding renaissance in the 1700s, marked by the crossing of ancient wild Chinese roses and old European cultivars—plants selectively bred through human intervention to develop a desirable characteristic.
Currently, we have over 150 to 200 species of roses and more than 35,000 cultivars, displaying a wide range of blooming frequencies, fragrances, and colors. However, global climate change has prompted rose breeders to shift their focus from purely cosmetic traits to breeding rose varieties that are more resistant to stress factors like drought, disease and easier to care for.
Borrowing genetic resources from wild rose varieties, which offer valuable traits such as fragrance and
disease resistance
, presents a promising strategy for breeding resilient, low-maintenance rose cultivars.
Genome sequencing of 205 samples representing 84 species reveal evolutionary and geographical history of the Rosa genus. Credit:
Nature Plants
(2025). DOI: 10.1038/s41477-025-01955-5
A clear understanding of the origin and evolution of the Rosa genus, both wild and cultivated varieties, can not only advance the breeding efforts but also aid in the conservation of near-threatened rose varieties.
Having this in mind, the researchers collected 205 samples of over 80 Rosa species, covering 84% of what is documented in the "Flora of China."
The samples were then analyzed using genomic sequencing,
population genetics
, and other methods to trace back their ancestral traits. They studied 707 single-copy genes uncovered as a set of conserved
genetic markers
like single-nucleotide polymorphisms—the most common type of genetic variation found in DNA—which helped them chart the evolutionary and geographical history and connections between the rose species.
Ancestral trait reconstruction showed that the shared ancestor of the studied samples was a yellow flower with a single row of petals and leaves divided into seven leaflets. As roses evolved and were domesticated, they developed new colors, distinct petal markings, and the ability to bloom in clusters.
The study also brought new insight to the widely accepted notion that the Rosa genus originated in Central Asia. The
genetic evidence
pointed to two major centers of
rose
diversity in China—one in the dry northwest, where yellow roses with small leaves grow, and another in the warm and humid southwest, where the white, fragrant variety thrives.
The researchers highlight that these findings provide a strong foundation for utilizing wild Rosa resources, which could assist in the re-domestication and innovative breeding of modern roses.
More information:
Bixuan Cheng et al, Phenotypic and genomic signatures across wild Rosa species open new horizons for modern rose breeding,
Nature Plants
(2025).
DOI: 10.1038/s41477-025-01955-5
Valéry Malécot, An evolutionary bouquet for roses,
Nature Plants
(2025).
DOI: 10.1038/s41477-025-01971-5

data.title: How to vibe code for free: Running Qwen3 on your Mac, using MLX
data.author: avetiszakharyan
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在MacBook上免费使用MLX运行Qwen3模型并通过Localforge实现自主代码生成。具体步骤包括安装MLX库和LLM辅助库，运行Qwen3模型服务器，配置Localforge以使用Qwen3模型及Ollama提供的辅助模型。完成设置后，用户可以通过自定义代理使用Qwen3模型执行任务，如运行LS工具显示文件夹内容，甚至创建自我运行的游戏。尽管需要一些实验和调整，但整个过程免费，且能在Mac上自主生成代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：本地运行大型语言模型（LLM）的体验与应用

不同观点：
• [积极评价] omneity认为Qwen3-30B-A3B在本地运行表现惊艳，速度和实用性都达到了非常可用的水平，尤其是0.6B模型在非trivial任务中的表现让人印象深刻。该用户正在评估其与现有系统的集成。
• [对比观点] bitbasher认为传统的"vibe coding"只需要简单的工具（如耳机和咖啡），成本低廉且有效，暗示不一定需要依赖高级工具如Qwen3。
• [批评与质疑] artdigital质疑Qwen3是否能真正实现"vibe coding"，认为其在处理多文件、目录导航等自主任务时表现不足，且怀疑相关言论是为localforge打广告。
• [经济考量] 999900000999指出，尽管付费模型表现更好，但本地运行模型具有成本优势，特别是在长期使用中可以通过购买硬件节省开支。不过对Ollama目前的表现有些失望。
• [技术问题] rcarmo提到Qwen3在处理某些提示时出现循环问题，而其他模型如mistral-small表现更好，暗示本地模型在代码生成方面仍有不足。

补充讨论：
• [工具与技术] kamranjon和nico关注本地调优工具和多模态模型的应用。nico特别提到希望了解如何在localforge中组合使用多个代理模型。
• [硬件需求与限制] jononor和Tacite讨论了硬件限制，尤其是VRAM大小对运行大模型的影响，指出当前硬件可能还不足以支持所有应用场景。
• [利益披露] walthamstow提醒用户注意Localforge可能是讨论者自己的项目，暗示可能存在利益相关。
• [技术细节] freeone3000指出教程中关于模型名称设置的重要性，避免404错误。
• [代理与记录] ttoinou提出希望有一个中央代理来统一管理本地和在线LLM服务，并记录LLM调用，以简化使用体验。
• [等待技术进步] endlessvoid94认为本地模型在编码任务中仍不足，目前仍依赖Sonnet 3.7，等待未来技术进步。

争议焦点：
• 本地模型是否能在自主任务中取代传统工具和付费模型。
• Localforge的宣传是否客观公正，是否涉及利益冲突。
• 本地运行大模型在硬件需求和实用性方面的争议。

43856489.article_content:
Running Qwen3 on your macbook, using MLX, to vibe code for free
(or how to Vibe code for free!)
Published: 1 May 2025
Today I wanted to test running Qwen3 latest models locally on my mac, and putting that in an agentic loop using localforge.
(or how to Vibe code for free!)
Qwen3 turns out to be a quite capable model available on ollama:
https://ollama.com/library/qwen3
And also on mlx community:
https://huggingface.co/collections/mlx-community/qwen3-680ff3bcb446bdba2c45c7c4
Feel free to grab a model of your choice depending on mac hardware and let's dive in.
Here is what I did step by step:
Step 1: Install the core MLX library
pip install mlx
Copy
Step 2: Install the LLM helper library
pip install mlx-lm
Copy
Step 3: Run the model server
mlx_lm.server --model mlx-community/Qwen3-30B-A3B-8bit --trust-remote-code --port 8082
Copy
This command will both download and serve it (change port to whatever you want, and be ready to download tens of gigabytes of stuff)
After download is done you should see something like:
2025-05-01 13:56:26,964 - INFO - Starting httpd at 127.0.0.1 on port 8082...
Meaning your model is ready to receive requests. Time to configure it in localforge!
Configure Localforge
Get your latest localforge copy at
https://localforge.dev
(either npm install for any platform or if you want there are DMG and ZIP files available for OSX and Windows)
Once running open settings and set it up like this:
1) In provider list add provider
I have added two providers: one is ollama for a weak model, and another is for mlx qwen3
a) Ollama provider settings:
Choose name:
LocalOllama
Choose
ollama
from provider types
No settings required
Important prerequisite:
You need to have ollama installed on your machine with some sort of model serving, preferably gemma3:latest
Install instructions for this are here:
https://ollama.com/library/gemma3
This model is needed for simple gerund and aux interactions such as for agent to figure out what is going on, but not serious stuff.
b) Qwen provider settings:
Choose any provider name such as
qwen3:mlx:30b
Choose
openai
as provider type, because we are going to be using openai api v1
For API key put something like
"not-needed"
For API url put:
http://127.0.0.1:8082/v1/
(note the port you used in previous steps)
2) Create a custom agent
After you made your provider, make custom agent!
Go to agents tab in settings and click +Add Agent,
type in some name, like
qwen3-agent
And then click pencil icon to edit your agent.
This will open a huge window, in it
you care about Main and Auxiliary cards at top (ignore the Expert card, can be anything or empty)
For
Main
put in your qwen provider, and as model name type in:
mlx-community/Qwen3-30B-A3B-8bit
(or whatever you downloaded from the mlx community)
For
Auxiliary
, choose your LocalOllama provider, and for model put in
gemma3:latest
You can leave agent prompt same for now, although it may make sense to simplify it for qwen.
In the tool sections you can unselect browser tools to make it more simple, although this is optional.
Using Your New Agent
Now that this is done, press command+s, and close the agent editor, and then close settings.
You should appear in the main chat window, in it on very top
there is select box saying - select agent.
Choose your new agent (qwen3-agent)
Your agent is ready to use tools!
I typed in something simple like:
"use LS tool to show me files in this folder"
And it did!
Qwen3 successfully running the LS tool through Localforge
And here's a website created by Qwen3:
A website created by Qwen3 using Localforge
It even made a snake game that plays itself!
A self-playing snake game created by Qwen3
Conclusion
This may require a bit more experimenting such as simplifying system prompt, or tinkering with mlx settings and model choices,
but I think this is definitely possible to use to get some autonomous code generation on YOUR MAC, totally free of charge!
Happy tinkering!
Published 1 May 2025

• [积极评价] omneity认为Qwen3-30B-A3B在本地运行表现惊艳，速度和实用性都达到了非常可用的水平，尤其是0.6B模型在非trivial任务中的表现让人印象深刻。该用户正在评估其与现有系统的集成。
• [对比观点] bitbasher认为传统的"vibe coding"只需要简单的工具（如耳机和咖啡），成本低廉且有效，暗示不一定需要依赖高级工具如Qwen3。
• [批评与质疑] artdigital质疑Qwen3是否能真正实现"vibe coding"，认为其在处理多文件、目录导航等自主任务时表现不足，且怀疑相关言论是为localforge打广告。
• [经济考量] 999900000999指出，尽管付费模型表现更好，但本地运行模型具有成本优势，特别是在长期使用中可以通过购买硬件节省开支。不过对Ollama目前的表现有些失望。
• [技术问题] rcarmo提到Qwen3在处理某些提示时出现循环问题，而其他模型如mistral-small表现更好，暗示本地模型在代码生成方面仍有不足。

补充讨论：
• [工具与技术] kamranjon和nico关注本地调优工具和多模态模型的应用。nico特别提到希望了解如何在localforge中组合使用多个代理模型。
• [硬件需求与限制] jononor和Tacite讨论了硬件限制，尤其是VRAM大小对运行大模型的影响，指出当前硬件可能还不足以支持所有应用场景。
• [利益披露] walthamstow提醒用户注意Localforge可能是讨论者自己的项目，暗示可能存在利益相关。
• [技术细节] freeone3000指出教程中关于模型名称设置的重要性，避免404错误。
• [代理与记录] ttoinou提出希望有一个中央代理来统一管理本地和在线LLM服务，并记录LLM调用，以简化使用体验。
• [等待技术进步] endlessvoid94认为本地模型在编码任务中仍不足，目前仍依赖Sonnet 3.7，等待未来技术进步。

争议焦点：
• 本地模型是否能在自主任务中取代传统工具和付费模型。
• Localforge的宣传是否客观公正，是否涉及利益冲突。
• 本地运行大模型在硬件需求和实用性方面的争议。

data.title: NASA's Psyche spacecraft hits a speed bump on the way to a metal asteroid
data.author: lisa_k
data.article_summary: NASA's Psyche spacecraft, on a mission to explore a metal-rich asteroid, has temporarily halted its engines due to a fuel pressure drop in its propulsion system. The issue, detected on April 1, caused the spacecraft to shut off its plasma thrusters. Engineers are investigating the cause, and there is currently no impact on the spacecraft's trajectory. Psyche uses solar electric propulsion with xenon gas and can coast until mid-June before potential drift. The mission, launched in October 2023, aims to reach the asteroid Psyche in 2029, with a total cost exceeding $1.4 billion. The asteroid, one of only nine metal-rich asteroids known, remains largely unexplored.

不同观点：

• [accrual的观点] 表达了对Psyche团队的祝福，并对出现问题时已经有冗余方案可以解决表示兴奋，显示出对NASA团队处理技术问题能力的信任和积极态度。

NASA's Psyche spacecraft, located nearly 150 million miles from Earth on the way to an unexplored metal asteroid, has stopped firing its engines after detecting a problem in its propulsion system.
NASA
published an update Tuesday
revealing that the robotic spacecraft shut off its plasma thrusters earlier this month. The news wasn't widely shared until Wednesday, when NASA science chief
Nicky Fox posted it on X
.
"Engineers with NASA’s Psyche mission are working to determine what caused a recent decrease in fuel pressure in the spacecraft’s propulsion system," the agency said. The spacecraft detected the drop in pressure April 1 inside the line that feeds xenon fuel to the spacecraft's four plasma thrusters.
Sensors aboard the Psyche probe detected a pressure reduction in the xenon fuel line from about 36 pounds per square inch to about 26 psi. "As designed, the orbiter powered off the thrusters in response to the decrease," NASA said.
The Psyche spacecraft uses solar electric propulsion, a highly efficient means of maneuvering through space that relies on solar-generated electricity and more than a ton of xenon gas stored in seven 22-gallon (82-liter) tanks. Inside each of the mission's four thrusters, an electromagnetic field ionizes the xenon gas before expelling the ions to produce thrust.
These things happen
Louise Prockter, director of NASA's planetary science division, said engineers at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California are looking into the problem.
So far, there's no effect on the Psyche spacecraft's trajectory. Psyche's plasma thrusters can remain unpowered until at least mid-June before the spacecraft would begin to drift off course, according to NASA. Mission managers decided to keep Psyche's engines turned off until they better understand the pressure decrease. If engineers trace the problem to the fuel line itself, NASA has the option of switching to a backup fuel line to resume thrusting.
"This kind of thing happens, and that’s why we build redundancy into our missions," Prockter said at a meeting of Mars scientists Wednesday. "We don't have any concerns at the moment about it, but we’re obviously keeping tabs on it.”
An illustration depicts a NASA spacecraft approaching the metal-rich asteroid Psyche. Though there are no plans to mine Psyche, such asteroids are being eyed for their valuable resources.
Credit:
NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU
Each electric thruster on Psyche generates just 250 milli-newtons of thrust, roughly equivalent to the weight of three quarters. But they can operate for months at a time, and over the course of a multi-year cruise, these thrusters provide a more efficient means of propulsion than conventional rockets.
The plasma thrusters are reshaping the Psyche spacecraft's path toward its destination, a metal-rich asteroid also named Psyche. The spacecraft's four electric engines, known as Hall effect thrusters, were supplied by a Russian company named Fakel. Most of the other components in Psyche's propulsion system—controllers, xenon fuel tanks, propellant lines, and valves—come from other companies or the spacecraft's primary manufacturer, Maxar Space Systems, in California.
The Psyche mission is heading first for Mars, where the spacecraft will use the planet's gravity next year to slingshot itself into the asteroid belt, setting up for arrival and orbit insertion around the asteroid Psyche in August 2029.
Psyche
launched in October 2023
aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket on the opening leg of a six-year sojourn through the Solar System. The mission's total cost adds up to more than $1.4 billion, including development of the spacecraft and its instruments, the launch, operations, and an
experimental laser communications package
hitching a ride to deep space with Psyche.
Psyche, the asteroid, is the size of Massachusetts and circles the Sun in between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter. No spacecraft has visited Psyche before. Of the approximately 1 million asteroids discovered so far, scientists say only nine have a metal-rich signature like Psyche. The team of scientists who put together the Psyche mission have little idea of what to expect when the spacecraft gets there in 2029.
Metallic asteroids like Psyche are a mystery. Most of Psyche's properties are unknown other than estimates of its density and composition. Predictions about the look of Psyche's craters, cliffs, and color have inspired artists to create a cacophony of illustrations, often showing sharp spikes and grooves alien to rocky worlds.
In a little more than five years, assuming NASA gets past Psyche's propulsion problem, scientists will supplant speculation with solid data.
Stephen Clark

data.title: Two publishers and three authors fail to understand what "vibe coding" means
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: Simon Willison批评两本即将出版的书以及其作者和出版社错误地使用了“vibe coding”这一术语。根据Andrej Karpathy的定义，“vibe coding”指的是完全依赖AI生成代码，而不关心代码本身，适用于一次性项目，而非专业生产代码。然而，这些书却将“vibe coding”误解为在专业软件开发中使用AI工具。Willison强调，真正的“vibe coding”应针对非软件开发者，帮助他们安全、有效地解决日常问题。他对这些作者和出版社未仔细理解该术语的完整定义感到失望，并指出这不仅造成了误解，还错失了一个有潜力的市场机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“vibe coding”这一新术语的定义、使用和影响的讨论

不同观点：
• 支持演变观点：[billy99k]认为“vibe coding”的定义已经随着社区影响和社交媒体的传播发生了变化，类似于黑客/骇客的辩论。这种变化是自然的，由最有影响力的群体定义。
• 营销视角：[everybodyknows]指出出版商可能只是为了营销目的使用“AI-Assisted Programming”或“Vibe Coding”这样的术语，而不关心技术话语的连贯性。
• 担忧未来编程方式：[firefoxd]担心“vibe coding”成为主流后，编程本身可能会变得 irrelevant，因为人类不再需要直接编写代码，而是通过与AI互动完成任务。
• 怀疑与批评：[rzz3]对“vibe coding”一词的创造时间提出质疑，认为其使用时间早于某些作者声称的时间。[zelon88]质疑一本不涉及实际编码的编程书籍是否由人类撰写。
• 名称争议：[davidhunter]认为“vibe coding”这个名称不够明确，建议使用“apping”作为替代。[puff_pastry]则认为一个词语可以有多重定义，不必拘泥于单一解释。

补充讨论：
• 实际操作疑问：[alabastervlog]希望看到一个展示“vibe coding”实际操作的视频，以更好地理解这一概念。[theflyestpilot]通过一个短故事解释了非开发者如何理解“vibe coding”，将其比作使用工具进行编程。
• 幽默与讽刺：[bitbasher]和[throwup238]以讽刺的方式表达了对“vibe coding”突然流行的不解和批评。[pchristensen]和[xnorswap]则通过引用其他作品和名言，表达了对术语演变的无奈或接受。

争议焦点：
• “vibe coding”的定义和使用是否合理，以及其对未来编程方式的影响。
• 术语命名的适当性及其对技术社区话语连贯性的影响。

Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Two publishers and three authors fail to understand what “vibe coding” means
1st May 2025
Vibe coding
does not mean “using AI tools to help write code”. It means “generating code with AI without caring about the code that is produced”. See
Not all AI-assisted programming is vibe coding
for my previous writing on this subject. This is a hill I am willing to die on. I fear it will be the death of me.
I just learned about not one but
two
forthcoming books that use vibe coding in the title and abuse that very clear definition!
Vibe Coding
by Gene Kim and Steve Yegge (published by IT Revolution) carries the subtitle “Building Production-Grade Software With GenAI, Chat, Agents, and Beyond”—exactly what vibe coding is not.
Vibe Coding: The Future of Programming
by Addie Osmani (published by O’Reilly Media) likewise talks about how professional engineers can integrate AI-assisted coding tools into their workflow.
I fear it may be too late for these authors and publishers to fix their embarrassing mistakes: they’ve already designed the cover art!
I wonder if this a new record for the time from a term being coined to the first published books that use that term entirely incorrectly.
Vibe coding was only coined by Andrej Karpathy on February 6th, 84 days ago. I will once again quote
Andrej’s tweet
, with my own highlights for emphasis:
There’s a new kind of coding I call “vibe coding”, where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and
forget that the code even exists
. It’s possible because the LLMs (e.g. Cursor Composer w Sonnet) are getting too good. Also I just talk to Composer with SuperWhisper so I barely even touch the keyboard.
I ask for the dumbest things like “decrease the padding on the sidebar by half” because I’m too lazy to find it. I “Accept All” always, I don’t read the diffs anymore. When I get error messages I just copy paste them in with no comment, usually that fixes it. The code grows beyond my usual comprehension, I’d have to really read through it for a while. Sometimes the LLMs can’t fix a bug so I just work around it or ask for random changes until it goes away.
It’s not too bad for throwaway weekend projects, but still quite amusing
. I’m building a project or webapp, but it’s not really coding—I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, and copy paste stuff, and it mostly works.
Andrej could not have stated this more clearly: vibe coding is when you
forget that the code even exists
, as a fun way to build
throwaway projects
. It’s not the same thing as using LLM tools as part of your process for responsibly building production code.
I know it’s harder now that tweets are longer than 480 characters, but it’s vitally important you
read to the end of the tweet
before publishing a book about something!
Now what do we call books on about real vibe coding?
This is the aspect of this whole thing that most disappoints me.
I think there is a real need for a book on
actual
vibe coding: helping people who are
not
software developers—and who don’t want to become developers—learn how to use vibe coding techniques
safely, effectively and responsibly
to solve their problems.
This is a rich, deep topic! Most of the population of the world are never going to learn to code, but thanks to vibe coding tools those people now have a path to building custom software.
Everyone deserves the right to automate tedious things in their lives with a computer. They shouldn’t have to learn programming in order to do that.
That
is who vibe coding is for. It’s not for people who are software engineers already!
There are so many questions to be answered here. What kind of projects can be built in this way? How can you avoid the traps around security, privacy, reliability and a
risk of over-spending
? How can you navigate the jagged frontier of things that can be achieved in this way versus things that are completely impossible?
A book for people like that could be a genuine bestseller! But because three authors and the staff of two publishers didn’t read to the end of the tweet we now need to find a new buzzy term for that, despite having the
perfect
term for it already.
I’m fully aware that I’ve lost at this point—
Semantic Diffusion
is an unstoppable force. What next? A book about prompt injection that’s
actually about jailbreaking
?
I’d like the publishers and authors responsible to at least understand how much potential value—in terms of both helping out more people and making more money—they have left on the table because they didn’t read all the way to the end of the tweet.

data.title: In the US, not even $11,000 a month can buy you dignity at the end of your life
data.author: howard941
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者父亲在高端养老院的糟糕经历，尽管每月支付高达11,000美元，老人仍未得到应有的关怀和尊严。作者的父亲是一位96岁的退休医生，在养老院中多次跌倒且无人照料，身体和精神状况迅速恶化。养老院员工不足，护理质量低下，与宣传的美好环境相差甚远。作者的母亲曾是科罗拉多州养老院居民权益的代言人，精心规划了父母的晚年生活，但突发情况打乱了计划。作者质疑当前以盈利为导向的养老体系，呼吁社会关注老年人的尊严和生活质量问题。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

43858663.article_content:
Social care
In the US, not even $11,000 a month can buy you dignity at the end of your life
After watching my father’s struggle in a system that values profit over compassion, I wonder: how much longer will we accept a future where most of us lose our sense of human worth in old age?
Laura Fraser
Thu 1 May 2025 09.00 EDT
Last modified on Thu 1 May 2025 09.01 EDT
Share
View image in fullscreen
Illustration: Rita Liu/The Guardian/Fraser Family/Getty
The last time I visited my father, I walked into his $11,000-a-month room in a posh assisted living residence and found him curled up on the floor. My sister Amy and I knelt down, touched him, and asked if he was okay.
“I don’t know,” mumbled Dad, 96, a retired physician and lifelong outdoorsman. “I fell about 20 minutes ago and no one has come.”
I went for help. Out in the common area, there were no caregiving staff anywhere. I found an administrator and the nurse, who came and briskly hoisted him into his easy chair, where he’d spent most of his time staring out the window at a slice of the mountains. Then they left.
I hugged Dad and noticed he was bleeding profusely from a skin tear on his arm. The nurse hadn’t so much as given him a quick once-over. He sat there dazed, his face stubbled, wearing the same stained and rumpled shirt he’d had on for most of the week, even though until his recent move to the facility he had always been impeccably groomed. He had already fallen several times while at the facility, often while trying to make it to the toilet when no one came to help him, or sliding out of bed. Sometimes, he hit his head.
His cognitive and physical decline in just two months had been dramatic. Though he’d been living on his own in a senior community, recent falls and dementia had made it unsafe for him to continue to live alone. My two sisters and I attributed some of his rapid downturn to the falls, and some, perhaps, to the sleep medications the staff been doling out at 6pm, presumably so they didn’t have to deal with him during his often-confused “
sundown syndrome
” hours in the evening.
This indifferent care belied the promises of the establishment’s website, which portrayed a warm and engaging environment where caregivers chatted with residents and offered companionship and comfort: “Your care team is always on hand to help – as little or as much as you need.”
Instead, Cindy had to visit for hours every day to help Dad, trying to prod administrators and overworked staff to give him more of the promised care for which we were paying dearly, but without making so much fuss that they’d evict him. She was stressed, and we were all heartbroken that aside from family visits, Dad was spending his last days lonely, helpless and bored, at the mercy of a company that seemed to be doing more warehousing than care.
After a lifetime of helping others as a ship’s doctor in the navy, a pediatrician, a physician on Native American reservations and a volunteer for numerous organizations, he deserved better.
View image in fullscreen
Charles Fraser, MD, was a ship’s doctor and lieutenant in the navy in the early 1950s.
Photograph: Picasa/Courtesy of the Fraser Family
Perhaps we shouldn’t have been surprised. Our late mother had spent her career advocating for the rights of nursing home and assisted living residents as the long-term care ombudsman for the state of
Colorado
. She knew everything about the industry – the good, the ugly – and had tried to set up my parents’ end-of-life plan to be the best possible for their quality of life.
After she learned she had Parkinson’s disease, she convinced Dad to sell their home of 40 years to buy into a continuing care retirement community with landscaped gardens, sweeping mountain views, several dining rooms, and a wide array of activities. They had an independent apartment, but Mom knew she might eventually need to move to assisted living while Dad stayed “home” nearby. Instead, she died suddenly of an enormous stroke – mercifully, it now seems – and left Dad living alone in his independent living apartment for the next 13 years.
Dad developed memory difficulties in his 90s – “Perfectly normal for my age,” he’d chuckle – and would occasionally fall, though he still exercised every day. Fiercely independent, he resisted hiring a health aide. At 96, a serious fall landed him in the hospital, and then a Medicare-reimbursed rehabilitation unit. After two weeks, the staff pronounced him ready to leave, but said he would require full-time skilled nursing to stay in his apartment, at over $1,000 a day. Frugal, and comfortably well-off but not wealthy, Dad balked. We asked the continuing care community to move him to the assisted living section on the premises, as the contract promised. But there was no room at the inn, and a long waiting list. That hadn’t been part of my parents’ plan.

data.author: mathgenius
data.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了自然语言处理（NLP）领域的巨大变革，特别是由于transformer模型和大型语言模型（LLM）的出现所引发的范式转变。2017年，Google研究人员提出了transformer模型，尽管最初并未被广泛认可，但其在NLP领域的潜力很快显现。2019年，BERT模型的推出标志着一个重要里程碑，随后LLM技术迅速普及，带来了科学发现、行业颠覆和广泛讨论。文章通过采访19位NLP研究人员，展示了这一技术变革对他们的影响，从最初的怀疑到逐渐接受，甚至有人经历了“存在危机”。这场变革不仅改变了NLP领域，也对整个AI社区产生了深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大语言模型（LLMs）对传统自然语言处理（NLP）方法的影响以及学术界的反应

不同观点：
• teruakohatu：认为LLMs让许多传统NLP研究变得过时，但传统方法在成本和特定任务上仍有优势。例如，VADER模型在情感分析中虽然有缺陷，但比LLMs便宜得多。传统NLP不会编造信息，也不会被“越狱”。
• AndrewKemendo：质疑Chomsky的语言结构假设，认为 intelligence 可以通过解决马尔可夫过程等方法实现，而无需语言结构。LLMs展示了语言并非智能的唯一基础。
• languagehacker：对AI和LLMs持保留态度，基于过去的经验，不信任这些模型的可靠性，并担心其潜在的负面影响。
• vjerancrnjak：指出在LLMs之前，CNNs已经在计算机视觉领域实现了飞跃，而Transformers在NLP中的出现也使得许多低级任务变得不必要。
• gitroom：表达了对旧有工作被迅速淘汰的失望和痛苦。
• softwaredoug：好奇LLMs对语言学和普遍语法概念的影响。
• ukuina：提醒大家AlexNet对计算机视觉领域的影响，暗示当前NLP领域的变革并不新鲜。
• o11c：质疑LLMs是否能可靠地处理否定词“not”，认为这是相较传统NLP的退步。
• jsemrau：对比FiNER、GliNER和Smolagents与本地运行的LLM，认为LLM效果更好。
• Animats：幽默地指出拥有终身教职在变革时期的重要性。
• sp1nningaway：作为外行，觉得文章杂乱，学术界的反应充满情感和政治色彩，没人对领域快速进展感到高兴。
• criddell：简单指出讨论的领域是自然语言处理。
• g42gregory：认为传统NLP方法将逐渐被LLMs或其后续模型重新吸收，LLMs仍有改进空间，中国等国家将推动更小、更高效的模型。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是LLMs是否彻底淘汰了传统NLP方法。teruakohatu和vjerancrnjak等认为传统方法仍有其优势和应用场景。
• 另一个焦点是对LLMs的可靠性和潜在影响的质疑，languagehacker和AndrewKemendo等对此持保留态度，担心其在实际应用中的表现。
• 讨论还涉及LLMs对语言学理论（如普遍语法）的影响，以及这些模型在处理特定语言特征（如否定词“not”）时的表现。
• 成本和效率是另一个重要讨论点，teruakohatu和g42gregory等都提到了LLMs的高成本问题及其可能的解决方案。

When ChatGPT Broke an Entire Field: An Oral History
By
John Pavlus
April 30, 2025
Researchers in “natural language processing” tried to tame human language. Then came the transformer.
Comment
Save Article
Read Later
James O’Brien for
Quanta Magazine
Something very significant has happened to the field.
And also to people.
—Christopher Potts
By
John Pavlus
Contributing Writer
April 30, 2025
View PDF/Print Mode
artificial intelligence
computer science
machine learning
natural language processing
neural networks
All topics
A
sking scientists to identify a paradigm shift, especially in real time, can be tricky. After all, truly ground-shifting updates in knowledge may take decades to unfold. But you don’t necessarily have to invoke the P-word to acknowledge that one field in particular —
natural language processing
, or NLP — has changed. A lot.
The goal of natural language processing is right there on the tin: making the unruliness of human language (the “natural” part) tractable by computers (the “processing” part). A blend of engineering and science that dates back to the 1940s, NLP gave Stephen Hawking a voice, Siri a brain and social media companies another way to target us with ads. It was also ground zero for the emergence of large language models — a technology that NLP helped to invent but whose explosive growth and transformative power still managed to take many people in the field entirely by surprise.
To put it another way: In 2019,
Quanta
reported on a then-groundbreaking
NLP system called BERT
without once using the phrase “large language model.” A mere five and a half years later, LLMs are everywhere, igniting discovery, disruption and debate in whatever scientific community they touch. But the one they touched first — for better, worse and everything in between — was natural language processing. What did that impact feel like to the people experiencing it firsthand?
Quanta
interviewed 19 current and former NLP researchers to tell that story. From experts to students, tenured academics to startup founders, they describe a series of moments — dawning realizations, elated encounters and at least one “existential crisis” — that changed their world. And ours.
* * *
Prologue: Before the Flood
transformers • BERTology • scale
By 2017,
neural networks
had already changed the status quo in NLP. But that summer, in a now-seminal paper titled “
Attention Is All You Need
,” researchers at Google introduced an entirely new kind of neural network called the transformer that would soon dominate the field. Not everyone saw it coming.
ELLIE PAVLICK
(assistant professor of computer science and linguistics, Brown University; research scientist, Google DeepMind)
:
Google had organized a workshop in New York for academics to hang out with their researchers, and Jakob Uszkoreit, one of the authors on that paper, was presenting on it. He was making a really clear point about how aggressively this model was not designed with any insights from language. Almost trolling a bit: I’m going to just talk about all these random decisions we made, look how absurd this is, but look how well it works.
There had already been a feeling of the neural nets taking over, and so people were very skeptical and pushing back. Everyone’s main takeaway was, “This is all just hacks.”
RAY MOONEY
(director, UT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, University of Texas at Austin)
:
It was sort of interesting, but it wasn’t an immediate breakthrough, right? It wasn’t like the next day the world changed. I really do think it’s not conceptually the right model for how to process language. I just didn’t realize that if you trained that very conceptually wrong model on a lot of data, it could do amazing things.
NAZNEEN RAJANI
(founder and CEO, Collinear AI; at the time a Ph.D. student studying with Ray Mooney)
:
I clearly remember reading “Attention Is All You Need” in our NLP reading group. Ray actually ran it, and we had this very lively discussion. The concept of
attention
had
been around for a while
, and maybe that’s why Ray’s reaction was kind of, “Meh.” But we were like, “Wow, this seems like a turning point.”
R. THOMAS MCCOY
(assistant professor, department of linguistics, Yale University)
:
During that summer, I vividly remember members of the research team I was on asking, “Should we look into these transformers?” and everyone concluding, “No, they’re clearly just a flash in the pan.”
Christopher Potts (chair, department of linguistics, Stanford University)
Courtesy of Christopher G. Potts
CHRISTOPHER POTTS
(chair, department of linguistics, Stanford Un

data.article_summary: Onyx International推出了售价1900美元的Boox Mira Pro彩色E Ink显示器，尺寸为25.3英寸，分辨率为3200×1800，采用E Ink Kaleido 3技术，能显示4096种颜色。尽管色彩和刷新率较传统显示器有妥协，但它专注于护眼文本和长续航。该显示器配有HDMI、mini HDMI、USB-C和DisplayPort接口，设计类似苹果的Studio Display，并支持VESA安装。与同类产品相比，Boox设备结合了E Ink优势和Google Play访问能力，设计上比Dasung的竞品更具吸引力。不过，美国买家需注意可能的进口关税问题，因显示器从香港发货。

不同观点：
• [qwerty456127] 认为当前的eInk显示器制造商过度追求高刷新率等参数以与传统显示器竞争，导致价格过高。他更希望购买便宜的、仅1 Hz刷新率的单色eInk显示器，用于阅读文本，而非观看视频等不适合eInk屏幕的任务。

• [JonChesterfield] 表示在英国难以找到此类产品的供应商，并提到在其他讨论中有人持反对意见。他个人认为在阳光下使用Emacs会很有效，并且有VESA支架可以固定迷你PC。他还提到欧洲商店因假期暂时不处理订单。

• [seam_carver] 认为当前的eInk显示器价格过高，决定继续使用Kindle和eInk手机。他分享了自己使用EinkBro浏览器和Ktool应用在eInk手机和Kindle上浏览Hacker News的体验，认为效果很好。

• [Beijinger] 表示不需要彩色显示，只需要一个便宜的20英寸eInk电脑屏幕。

• [CobaltFire] 提到之前在其他新闻平台上有过类似的讨论，提供了一个链接供参考。

• [addoo] 提到他已经知道有类似产品存在，但仍希望看到更多创新和竞争。他对eInk技术充满热情，并已购买了Dasung的便携式显示器用于个人阅读，但无法用于工作。

• [obayesshelton] 对eInk显示器的高价格表示惊讶，并好奇它们是否对眼睛更好。他认为这种价格不值得。

• [ChrisArchitect] 提到这是一个重复的讨论，并提供了一个链接。

• [daveguy] 提到在美国，eInk显示器的价格可能高达4,275美元，具体取决于关税由谁承担。他还提到批量进口时价格较低。

• [ta1243] 担心在美国购买时关税未包含在显示器价格中，并开玩笑提到这可能会影响到某些政治人物。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于eInk显示器的价格和功能优化方向。部分用户希望有更便宜、功能更简单的显示器，而制造商似乎更注重高刷新率和多功能性，导致价格上升。

• 关税和进口成本也是影响价格的重要因素，特别是在美国市场。
