data.title: Meta tightens privacy policy around Ray-Ban glasses to boost AI training
data.author: nickthegreek
data.article_summary: Meta对其Ray-Ban智能眼镜的隐私政策进行了调整，主要包括两点变化：首先，Meta AI和相机功能默认启用，除非用户关闭语音助手功能“Hey Meta”。其次，用户不再能选择禁止存储语音记录，但可以随时手动删除这些记录。这些更改旨在为AI模型训练提供更多数据支持。此前，用户在3月份已注意到这些变化，而政策在4月29日正式生效。Meta还计划在2025年发布更高端的Ray-Ban眼镜版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：智能眼镜的实际用途和其对周围人的影响

不同观点：
• [mmmlinux的观点] 认为智能眼镜的实用性不明确。虽然得到了一个二手的智能眼镜，但除了当作普通耳机使用或者识别植物外，没有发现其他实际用途。即便看了广告，发现广告内容也无法清晰展示智能眼镜的独特功能，感觉广告和普通太阳镜的广告差不多。

• [m463的观点] 提出智能眼镜可能对周围人产生影响。虽然没有直接讨论智能眼镜的个人用途，但指出需要考虑这种设备对周围人的影响，暗示智能眼镜可能在社交场合中对他人产生干扰或影响。

补充讨论：
• [mmmlinux]对智能眼镜广告的批评表明，目前市场对这种产品的定位和宣传可能存在问题，无法有效传达其核心价值。
• [m463]的评论引出了一个新的讨论维度，即智能设备不仅仅要考虑个人使用体验，还要考虑其在社交环境中的影响。这可能涉及到隐私问题、社交礼仪等。

争议焦点：智能眼镜的实际用途和其对周围人的影响是否被充分考虑和有效传达。

43858080.article_content:
News
Meta tightens privacy policy around Ray-Ban glasses to boost AI training
The company has removed the option to disable your voice recordings from being stored, among other changes.
The company has removed the option to disable your voice recordings from being stored, among other changes.
by
Chris Welch
Apr 30, 2025, 1:31 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge
Chris Welch
is a senior reviewer who has worked at The Verge since its founding in 2011. His coverage areas include audio (Sonos, Apple, Bose, Sony, etc.), home theater, smartphones, photography, and more.
Meta is making a few notable adjustments to the privacy policy for its Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses. In an email sent out on April 29th to owners of the glasses, the company outlined two key changes. First, “Meta AI with camera use is always enabled on your glasses unless you turn off ‘Hey Meta,” the email said; the latter refers to the hands-free voice command functionality.
That said, spokesperson Albert Aydin tells
The Verge
“the photos and videos captured on Ray-Ban Meta are on your phone’s camera roll and not used by Meta for training, including photos or videos captured by using the ‘Hey Meta, take a photo/video’ voice command. If you share those photos to a product — for example, Meta AI, cloud services or a third-party product — then the policies of that product will apply.“
Second, Meta is
taking after Amazon
by no longer allowing Ray-Ban Meta owners to opt out of having their voice recordings stored in the cloud. “The option to disable voice recordings storage is no longer available, but you can delete recordings anytime in settings,” the company wrote. In
its voice privacy notice
, Meta states that “voice transcripts and stored audio recordings are otherwise stored for up to one year to help improve Meta’s products.” If the company detects that a voice interaction was accidental, those recordings are deleted after a shorter 90-day window.
The motivation behind these changes is clear: Meta wants to continue providing its AI models with heaps of data on which to train and improve subsequent results. Some users began
noticing these policy changes in March
, but at least in the United States, Meta says they went into effect as of April 29th.
Earlier this month, the company
rolled out a live translation feature
to the Ray-Ban Meta product. And just yesterday, Meta rolled out a
standalone Meta AI app
on smartphones to more directly compete with Open AI’s ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Anthropic’s Claude, and other AI chatbots.
The company is reportedly planning
a higher-end pair of Ray-Ban Meta glasses
for release later in 2025. The current glasses lineup starts at $299, but the more premium version could cost around $1,000. Meta is set to report its Q1 2025 earnings later on Wednesday, and the company is likely to address the tariff chaos that has roiled markets in recent months.
Update April 30th, 6:00PM ET:
The article has been updated to clarify details and with a statement from Meta.

data.article_summary: 麦当劳报告称，2025年第一季度美国销售额出现自新冠疫情以来的最大跌幅，同比下降3.6%。尽管与《Minecraft》电影合作营销并推出优惠活动，顾客仍因对美国经济不确定性的担忧减少了光顾次数。首席执行官Chris Kempczinski表示，消费者正面临不确定性，但麦当劳将努力应对市场挑战。全球同店销售额下降1%，尽管在日本、澳大利亚和中东市场销售增长。同期，美国经济年化收缩0.3%，特朗普总统呼吁对经济表现保持耐心，并将销售下滑归因于“拜登经济”。企业与消费者对潜在的物价上涨和关税影响感到紧张，一些公司如英特尔和阿迪达斯表示关税将导致成本上升和价格提高。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：麦当劳的食品质量、价格变化、经营模式的变化以及外部因素（如通胀和政治因素）对其影响。

不同观点：
• **treebeard901**：麦当劳过去以低价提供真正的食物，但从90年代初开始，食物质量逐渐下降，用廉价原料替代，导致食物看似食物但实际并非如此。到2000年代，价格虽然低廉但质量低劣，如今组合餐价格甚至高达15美元，但食物质量并未改善。评论者认为麦当劳的经营模式是骗局，并建议公司高层应重新关注一线工作以改进服务。

• **taylodl**：麦当劳面临的最大问题是通货膨胀。其商业模式原本依赖于提供价格合理、快速且优质的食物，但现在“廉价”这一要素已经不再。此外，由于进口牛肉成本受关税影响增加，麦当劳陷入了经营困境。评论者指出，消费者只需多花几美元就能在其他地方获得更好的食物体验。

• **duxup**：质疑麦当劳的质量问题。过去，麦当劳在不同门店间的质量一致性较高，且员工看起来比其他快餐店更积极。但现在质量不稳定，有些门店员工明显缺乏动力，导致麦当劳不再像过去那样可靠。

• **evolve2k**：提到BDS运动对麦当劳销售的影响，指出由于麦当劳被认为支持以色列，许多国际消费者尤其是年轻人发起了抵制运动，导致麦当劳在国际市场上的销售增长乏力。评论者强调，虽然美国国内消费者可能不了解这一情况，但全球其他地方的消费者对美国品牌的支持正在减少。

• **Flatcircle**：指出麦当劳的价格已经高得令人震惊，尤其是对那些很久没光顾的顾客来说。

• **koksik202**：提到麦当劳的烹饪方式发生了变化，过去使用烤架制作新鲜食物，而现在大多是从塑料抽屉中取出预制食品进行简单加热，导致食物失去了原有的风味。相比之下，汉堡王仍然提供烤制肉饼的风味。

• **danielbln**：在欧洲中部地区，Burger King提供丰富的植物基食品选择，而麦当劳的植物基产品选择相对不足。因此，作为不吃肉的消费者，评论者更倾向于选择Burger King。

• **downrightmike**：提到“巨无霸指数”作为经济指标，指出麦当劳的巨无霸价格增长速度远超工资增长，可能对消费者造成影响，麦当劳应对此保持关注。

补充讨论：
• 麦当劳的全球经营面临多重挑战，包括通胀、关税、消费者抵制运动以及食品质量和价格问题。
• 不同地区的消费者对麦当劳的期望和体验有所不同，例如欧洲消费者更关注植物基食品选择。
• 麦当劳内部质量控制和员工动力的变化也被认为是其品牌形象和顾客体验下降的原因之一。

43859458.article_content:
McDonald's sales drop as diners face 'uncertainty'
4 hours ago
Share
Save
Mitchell Labiak
Business reporter, BBC News
Share
Save
Getty Images
McDonald's has suffered its biggest drop in US sales since the height of Covid, a fall that it said was driven by people's concerns over the US economy.
Despite a marketing tie-in with the Minecraft movie and extended price deals, US customers made fewer visits to the burger chain in the first three months of this year, compared to a year ago.
Chief executive Chris Kempczinski said customers were "grappling with uncertainty".
But he assured investors that the firm could "navigate even the toughest of market conditions".
McDonald's has been
working for months to try to reignite enthusiasm among customers
, after facing a backlash over rising prices, especially lower income households.
However, revenue at US McDonald's outlets that have been open at least a year sank 3.6% in the first three months of 2025 compared to a year earlier.
That is the steepest decline in like-for-like sales in the US since the three months to the end of June 2020 when pandemic restrictions were in place.
The surprise drop in sales coincided with a contraction in the US economy, which shrank at an annual rate of 0.3% in the first three months of 2025, the first quarterly decline in output since 2022.
Reacting to the growth figures, President Trump called for patience, saying he needed
"a little bit of time"
and described the numbers as a reflection of the "Biden economy", a reference to his predecessor as president.
However, Danni Hewson, head of financial analysis at AJ Bell, said Americans were nervous and cutting back on discretionary spending as a result.
"They're worried prices will rise even higher and that household budgets, already feeling the impact of previous inflation, will be stretched beyond breaking point," she said.
"They're also nervous about the potential for job losses if the economy continues to stutter as businesses try and make sense of an evolving tariff environment."
McDonald's figures reflect the first two months of Donald Trump's presidency, with the reporting period ending just before his barrage of tariff announcements on 2 April.
Dubbed "Liberation Day", that broadside prompted further confusion among many firms and consumers.
Mr Kempczinski said: "Consumers today are grappling with uncertainty, but they can always count on McDonald's [...] for exceptional value".
"McDonald's has a 70-year legacy of innovation, leadership, and proven agility, all of which give us confidence in our ability to navigate even the toughest of market conditions and gain market share," he added.
Over the same three-month period to March, the slump in McDonald's US sales dragged its global like-for-like revenue down 1%, despite growing sales in Japan, Australia, and the Middle East.
Higher prices
Businesses have had a mix of reactions since Trump began revealing and enforcing his plans for tariffs, which are a tax payable by a person or firm buying a good from overseas.
This week,
technology giant Intel said
costs would rise and a recession was more likely because of Trump's tariffs.
Sportswear brand Adidas said they would lead to
higher prices in the US for popular trainers including the Gazelle and Samba
.
Meanwhile, delivery giant DHL paused deliveries worth more than $800 (£603) due to US trade policy before
lifting them after negotiating "adjustments" to customs rues
.
Trump and his allies have said the policies will help to bring more jobs to the US as firms base factories and operations the country to avoid the new taxes.
However, many companies and economists have said this will be difficult to achieve and will likely mean job losses and economic pain at least in the short term.

data.article_summary: 美国洛杉矶港执行董事吉恩·塞罗卡（Gene Seroka）在2024年表示，由于美中贸易战，零售商的库存即将仅够维持约7周。贸易争端导致关税上升，供应链受阻，进口商品成本增加，库存压力加大。零售商面临库存短缺风险，可能影响商品供应和价格。塞罗卡警告，若局势持续，港口拥堵和物流问题将进一步恶化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于美国对华关税政策及其潜在经济影响的讨论

不同观点：
• **反对过度分析和关税政策的负面影响**：
   - [disqard] 认为对关税政策的过度分析是无意义的，因为不会产生任何有建设性的结果。
   - [Mr_Eri_Atlov] 预言美国经济将面临重大问题，因为当前政策不可持续。
   - [apricot] 批评两次选举“小丑”后抱怨出现混乱的人，暗示领导层选择问题。

• **关税政策的短期痛苦与长期收益**：
   - [toddmorey] 质疑是否有经济学家支持关税政策能带来长期经济利益，并指出像Jeff Ferry这样的少数声音存在，但他们的观点不适用于当前全球供应链现实。
   - [SkyMarshal] 认为与对手国家（如中国）脱钩是一个值得追求的目标，但需要更明智和渐进的政策，而非特朗普和纳瓦罗的“蛮干”方式，建议逐步增加关税，并结合其他经济工具，以减少对经济的破坏。

• **对供应链危机的担忧**：
   - [faefox] 警告当前库存耗尽后可能出现的严重供应链问题，并指出新供应链无法在短期内建立。
   - [Someone] 质疑为何6-7周的库存会被视为 alarming，并引用平均库存周转率数据来支持其观点。

• **对美国投资环境的担忧**：
   - [anon-3988] 认为美国政策的频繁变动（每四年一次）损害了其投资吸引力。

• **对社会态度和国际形象的批评**：
   - [qwertox] 引用推文批评美国人难以合作，并指出发达国家普遍存在类似问题。
   - [alkonaut] 认为当政府开始将经济指标归因于前一届时，是一个警示信号。

• **非传统解决方案和极端情景的讨论**：
   - [MaoSYJ] 提出一个假设，即毒品卡特尔可能利用其现有基础设施来解决物流问题，并多元化走私科技产品。

• **应对潜在短缺的建议**：
   - [tqi] 询问在可能出现类似COVID早期的短缺情况下，应该储备哪些基本物品。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到关税政策对美国经济的短期和长期影响，尤其是对供应链和投资环境的潜在破坏性影响。
• 对当前政策制定方式的批评，呼吁更渐进和多工具结合的经济政策，以减少负面效应。
• 讨论涉及对未来可能出现的极端经济和社会问题的猜测和应对策略。

• throwaw12认为Meta正试图进入AI云服务领域，以保持其在技术领域的领先地位，类似于AWS、Azure和GCP的成功。
• ahmedfromtunis质疑Llama模型在实际应用中的优势，表示尚未找到其比其他竞争模型更具优势的用例。
• wewewedxfgdf建议Meta开发特定领域的LLM模型，例如计算机编程，以提高模型的实用性和运行效率。

• hedayet对Meta的发布内容进行了详细分析，认为其创新性不足，且缺乏具体的数据支持，尤其对Llama API和Llama Stack的评价较低。
• amusingimpala75和nailer批评Meta的“开放源码”声明，指出其模型许可协议并非真正的开放源码，并质疑其开放性承诺。
• andhuman表达了对Meta未发布如Omni类型的多模态模型（支持语音输入输出）的失望。
• zoobab和scosman则关注实际操作问题，如无法访问等待名单和缺乏训练数据。

争议焦点：
• Meta是否真正致力于开放源码及其AI技术的开放性。
• Llama模型在实际应用中的竞争力和优势。
• Meta在AI技术发展中的商业策略和未来方向。

data.title: It's School time: Adventures in hacking an old Kindle
data.author: FlyingSnake
data.article_summary:
本文讲述了作者在一个周一早晨因女儿再次错过校车而引发的项目：将旧Kindle改造成一个上学准备仪表盘。首先，作者通过几步简单的操作成功越狱了Kindle，包括识别型号、安装WinterBreak、设置热修复、安装Kindle统一应用启动器和包安装器，以及通过USBNet包启用SSH。在解决了一些网络连接问题后，作者获得了Kindle的root访问权限。

接下来，作者开发了一个显示PNG图像的仪表盘应用，利用修改后的脚本定期从服务器获取图像并全屏显示。由于Kindle的限制，图像需为8位灰度格式，并匹配显示分辨率。

最后，作者设计了一个后端API，使用Cloudflare Workers、Hono JS、Cloudflare KV和Bun等工具处理实时数据并生成PNG图像。通过Pirate Weather API获取天气数据，作者完成了这个有趣的项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kindle的改造、使用和相关技术问题

不同观点：
• bigiain建议利用Kindle的电池信息控制智能插座，自动为设备充电，并分享了通过定时器为iPad节省费用的实际案例。
• shlip关注Kindle的越狱问题，询问哪种Kindle最容易在不注册的情况下越狱，并提到Windbreak需要设备注册的问题。
• mtlynch讨论了在Kindle仪表板模组中，为什么所有逻辑处理需要在外部服务器上进行，而不是在Kindle本地执行，并对Linux环境下的本地运行提出疑问。
• marcod分享了使用旧Kindle Fire的经历，提到设备无法更新导致无法安装当前应用的问题，并希望通过kindlemodding.org来解决。
• ishanmahapatra指出Winterbreak不支持最新的Kindle固件版本，且无法降级固件，除非设备之前已被越狱，因此需要等待新的越狱方法发布。

• dmitrygr和mahi_novice对天气预报显示四位小数的准确性表示幽默和赞赏。
• goodboyjojo对通过黑客技术和改造让旧设备焕发新生的做法表示赞赏。
• badmonster对文章中提到的cf-wasm图像处理和处理实际问题（如BVG strikes）表示赞赏。
• megous分享了Pocketbook创造者通过逆向工程实现的创新，如使用没有eInk接口的SoC驱动eInk显示面板。

43822251.article_content:
It was Monday and my daughter was late for the school again. To make things worse, the bus came early by 2 minutes. After rushing and making sure she caught the bus on time, I sat down for my morning coffee and opened up Hacker News. The front page had an interesting entry: “All Kindles can now be jailbroken”. Curiously my old kindle was lying next to me. Was this a sign from the universe? There was only one way to know and thus began my journey to turn my kindle into a get-ready-for-school dashboard.
Level 1: Jailbreaking the Kindle ⛓️‍💥
Jailbreaking the kindle was a relatively easy process. The fine folks at
kindlemodding.org
have created a user friendly guide with easy step by step instructions. The guide is very comprehensive and user friendly so it would be futile for me to repeat the steps here. The
KindModding Discord
community is also a great place to ask for troubleshooting.
In a nutshell the main steps I took to jailbreak my kindle were:
Identify your kindle model.
Install WinterBreak. (Just place the zip file in the kindle and reboot.)
Setup a hotfix, i.e. make sure the jailbreak persists after updates.
Install the Kindle Unified App Launcher and a package installer (MRPI)
Enable SSH on the Kindle using USBNet package.
Network shenanigans ☎️
I hit my first roadblock while setting up SSH access for the kindle. The standard USBNet package did not work for my kindle and after some research I found
USBNetLite
which got the SSH working.
The USBNetlite package enables connection to the kindle using 2 modes:
RNDIS/Ethernet gadget. This shows up as
usbx
(
usb0
in my case)
SSH over network using the IP address assigned by the router. This shows up as
wlanx
(
wlan0
in my case)
[root@kindle us]# ifconfig
lo        Link encap:Local Loopback
inet addr:127.0.0.1  Mask:255.0.0.0
...
usb0      Link encap:Ethernet  HWaddr EE:19:00:00:00:00
inet addr:192.168.15.244  Bcast:192.168.15.255  Mask:255.255.255.0
...
wlan0     Link encap:Ethernet  HWaddr 08:84:9D:7B:9C:F1
inet addr:192.168.2.71  Bcast:192.168.2.255  Mask:255.255.255.0
...
To enable the SSH network I had to do the following steps:
Enable USBNet from the KUAL Menu.
Set the IP address manually to
192.168.15.201
or any address in the
192.168.15.xxx
subnet.
SSH using
ssh 192.168.15.244
(usb0 ethernet interface) or the
wlan0
address assigned by the router.
Enter the password from the
/etc/config
file.
With this I had root access to the kindle 🥷
[root@kindle us]# uname -a
Linux kindle 4.1.15-lab126 #1 SMP PREEMPT Thu Nov 28 11:37:06 UTC 2024 armv7l GNU/Linux
Level 2: Conjuring a dashboard on the Kindle ✨
Kindle OS is stripped down version of Linux running an ancient kernel and old Gnu utilities but no package manager. The kindle has several custom tools that enable the Kindle UI operations, like the custom UI framework called
framework
and it’s side-kick
lab126_gui
. It’s workhorse is
lipc
, a
dbus
style program which is used to issue commands to drive the device operations.
There are several ways to develop an app for a hacked kindle. Some apps like KoReader use the FBInk framework
1
and some use Java applets
2
. I chose the easy path: disable the framework, display a PNG image periodically in full screen mode
3
.
I modified the main
dash.sh
script from the OG repos to match my needs. As it happens with old unmaintained devices, neither
xh
nor
wget
worked for my kindle in the background mode. After some debugging, I finally switched back to plain ‘ol
curl
to fetch the PNG from the backend API.
The script runs in a loop based on a cron schedules:
It stops the kindle UI frameworks and screensavers if they’re running.
It checks if the internet is accessible.
It fetches the PNG image from the server
It displays it fullscreen on the kindle using the
eips
command.
A Note about the image resolution: Kindle needs images in 8-bit Grayscale else it will not be displayed correctly. You will also need to find out the kindle’s display resolution using
eips -i
command. (Mine was 800x600)
I used a dummy image to test the kindle client before moving on to the backend side.
Level 3: The API server in the clouds 🌤️
I designed a backend API that collected the data in real-time data and exported it as a PNG image. For that I wanted a platform that’s always up, supports modern web standards, and has a pleasant developer experience. Cloudflare Developer Platform meets all the criteria and it was a breeze to get started.
I used the following tools/frameworks for my backend.
Cloudflare Workers: The workhorse to process incoming requests and image processing.
Hono JS: A Fast, lightweight JS framework.
Cloudflare KV: To cache network requests for an hour
Bun and TypeScript: I love Zig and Bun is really pleasant to work with.
Weather
I am a big fan of
Merry Sky
and the realtime weather API
Pirate Weather API
that powers it. After getting the API key, it was a matter of few hours to fine tune the data I needed to get current weather data. I loved that Cloudflare secrets make it very easy

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple II、Apple /// 设备的兼容性以及硬件与软件仿真的对比

不同观点：
• [rbanffy] 认为Apple II和Apple /// 的兼容性会很有吸引力。他基于使用C64 Maxi的经验指出，物理设备的外观和键盘等硬件因素在维持“这是 authentic（真正的）设备”的错觉中起到了重要作用，而不仅仅是完美的仿真软件。

• [ferguess_k] 对[rbanffy]的观点表示兴趣，但认为由于这类设备的目标用户多为技术人员，很多人可能会选择自己进行软件仿真，而不一定需要专门的硬件设备。他认为如果设备是原生支持而非仿真，会更有吸引力，但也会更昂贵。

补充讨论：
• [rbanffy] 强调了硬件的物理因素对用户体验的影响，尤其是对老设备的怀旧感。
• [ferguess_k] 则更关注技术用户的实际需求和经济性，认为原生硬件虽然更吸引人，但成本可能会更高。
• 争议的焦点在于，用户是否更在意硬件的物理仿真体验（如键盘、外观）还是更倾向于追求原生硬件或软件仿真的实际功能和性价比。

data.title: You Wouldn't Download a Hacker News
data.author: jasonthorsness
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者通过自建的Hacker News API客户端下载了整个网站的历史数据（约20GB的JSON文件），并使用DuckDB数据库对这些数据进行分析。作者详细描述了如何使用DuckDB查询不同编程语言（如Python、JavaScript、Java、Ruby和Rust）在Hacker News讨论中出现的频率变化，并生成了12周的移动平均值图表。作者认为DuckDB非常适合处理如此大规模的数据集，并调侃未来可能会用这些数据训练LLM模型来替代人类发言。最终，作者提供了分析过程的SQL代码，并邀请读者访问其项目网站。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何获取和使用Hacker News数据及其相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• [数据获取方式] montebicyclelo和flakiness提到可以使用BigQuery和ClickHouse直接查询Hacker News数据，无需下载，而userbinator则提到自己拥有一个20 GiB的JSON文件，并对数据量表示惊讶。byearthithatius讨论了通过递增item id来抓取HN数据的可能性，但指出了该方法的时间和请求数量问题。

• [数据使用和分析] mattkevan分享了自己通过下载Twitter/Bluesky数据并微调模型生成内容的经历，但对此感到有些失望。bambax担心有人会用HN数据训练机器人并取代人类贡献者。dredmorbius提到自己曾抓取HN首页存档，并发现评论提供了更多的文本数据以供分析。

• [技术建议和工具] jakegmaths指出Java查询中包含JavaScript实例的问题。g8oz预测未来API可能会直接返回duckdb文件。ashish01分享了自己的数据获取工具，并提出近期数据会比旧数据更快过时的观点。mike503希望有一个离线版本的数据，以备未来使用。

• [伦理和合法性] SilverBirch提出了下载HN数据的网络礼仪问题，质疑是否需要在抓取数据前获得许可。

• [数据可视化] stefs对堆叠图表的使用提出批评，认为这种图表容易误导读者并对数据产生错误印象。

• [历史讨论] 9rx和febeling讨论了Rust语言在发布前后的关注度变化，质疑其"崛起"的说法。

补充讨论：
• 评论中还涉及了对数据抓取和分析的技术细节、工具选择以及伦理问题的讨论，反映出社区对数据使用多样性和复杂性的关注。

. There are already a bunch of other
clients, but I wanted to try the latest Go features and linters on a new project. I’m glad I did; it
was a lot of fun.
The client can retrieve active items, lists of items, etc. (comments and stories are called “items”
in the
HN API
). Although I only really needed recent items for
my project, for completeness I added “scan” which downloads all the items, in order, from zero to
the latest or the other way around.
I wondered — could I just download the whole thing? Extrapolating from a few thousand items, it
would only be tens of GiB of JSON. I thought I’d give it a try.
hn scan --no-cache --asc -c- -o full.json
I had to CTRL-C a stalled download a few times, but scan is resumable so after a few hours I was
done. I had a 20 GiB JSON file of everything that has ever happened on Hacker News, and I can just
re-run the command above to “top it off” any time I need the latest. But what could I do with it?
Part 2: Feed The Ducks
First I just grepped for things. How many times has the phrase
“
correct horse battery staple
” appeared on the
site? Quite a few: 231 times (the last one
just today
). But grepping stuff is old news, so I
thought I’d try out DuckDB.
In the database world, DuckDB is unique: a super-fast embeddable analytics execution engine also
available as a command-line tool. I spend most of my day wrangling a
different database
(there’s the plug my coworkers will be looking
for) but I’ve been meaning to try DuckDB and it seemed perfect for this one-off task.
As it turns out, with their new UI for novices like me, it’s a breeze to use. AND LLMs are pretty
good at helping craft the SQL queries. I just had to import the data:

Now that I have a local download of all Hacker News content, I can train hundreds of LLM-based bots
on it and run them as contributors, slowly and inevitably replacing all human text with the output
of a chinese room oscillator perpetually echoing and recycling the past.
Or alternatively, I think for this project I am done. Someone else will have to take it to the next

data.title: An illustrated guide to automatic sparse differentiation
data.author: mariuz
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了自动稀疏微分（ASD）技术，旨在加速机器学习中Hessians和Jacobians的计算。尽管自动微分（AD）在机器学习中广泛应用，但ASD尚未普及。文章首先回顾了传统AD的基础，包括前向和反向模式下的Jacobians计算，然后深入探讨ASD的两个核心组件：稀疏模式检测和矩阵着色。文章还讨论了稀疏Hessians的计算，并通过实际演示展示了ASD的性能优势，提供了何时使用ASD而非AD的指导。ASD通过利用Hessians和Jacobians的稀疏性，显著提升了计算效率并减少了内存需求。

主要讨论点：关于Jacobian计算及其在自动微分（autodiff）中的应用的讨论

43828423.article_content:
An Illustrated Guide to Automatic Sparse Differentiation
In numerous applications of machine learning, Hessians and Jacobians exhibit sparsity, a property that can be leveraged to vastly accelerate their computation. While the usage of automatic differentiation in machine learning is ubiquitous, automatic sparse differentiation (ASD) remains largely unknown. This post introduces ASD, explaining its key components and their roles in the computation of both sparse Jacobians and Hessians. We conclude with a practical demonstration showcasing the performance benefits of ASD.
$$ \newcommand{\colorf}[1]{\textcolor{RoyalBlue}{#1}} \newcommand{\colorh}[1]{\textcolor{RedOrange}{#1}} \newcommand{\colorg}[1]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{#1}} \newcommand{\colorv}[1]{\textcolor{VioletRed}{#1}} \def\sR{\mathbb{R}} \def\vx{\mathbf{x}} \def\vv{\mathbf{v}} \def\vb{\mathbf{e}} \newcommand{\vvc}[1]{\colorv{\vv_{#1}}} \newcommand{\vbc}[1]{\colorv{\vb_{#1}}} \newcommand{\dfdx}[2]{\frac{\partial f_{#1}}{\partial x_{#2}}(\vx)} \newcommand{\J}[2]{J_{#1}(#2)} \def\Jf{\J{f}{\vx}} \def\Jg{\J{g}{\vx}} \def\Jh{\J{h}{g(\vx)}} \def\Jfc{\colorf{\Jf}} \def\Jgc{\colorg{\Jg}} \def\Jhc{\colorh{\Jh}} \newcommand{\D}[2]{D{#1}(#2)} \def\Df{\D{f}{\vx}} \def\Dg{\D{g}{\vx}} \def\Dh{\D{h}{g(\vx)}} \def\Dfc{\colorf{\Df}} \def\Dgc{\colorg{\Dg}} \def\Dhc{\colorh{\Dh}} $$
First-order optimization is ubiquitous in machine learning (ML) but second-order optimization is much less common. The intuitive reason is that high-dimensional vectors (gradients) are cheap, whereas high-dimensional matrices (Hessians) are expensive. Luckily, in numerous applications of ML to science or engineering,
Hessians and Jacobians exhibit sparsity
: most of their coefficients are known to be zero. Leveraging this sparsity can vastly
accelerate automatic differentiation
(AD) for Hessians and Jacobians, while decreasing its memory requirements
. Yet, while traditional AD is available in many high-level programming languages like Python
and Julia
,
automatic sparse differentiation (ASD) is not as widely used
. One reason is that the underlying theory was developed in the AD community, outside of the ML research ecosystem.
With this blog post, we aim to shed light on the inner workings of ASD, bridging the gap between the ML and AD communities by presenting well established techniques from the latter field. We start out with a short introduction to traditional AD, covering the computation of Jacobians in both forward and reverse mode. We then dive into the two primary components of ASD:
sparsity pattern detection
and
matrix coloring
. Having described the computation of sparse Jacobians, we move on to sparse Hessians.
After discussing applications in machine learning, we conclude with a practical demonstration of ASD, providing performance benchmarks and guidance on when to use ASD over AD.
Automatic differentiation
Let us start by covering the fundamentals of traditional AD. The reader can find more details in the recent book by Blondel and Roulet
, as well as Griewank and Walther
.
AD makes use of the
compositional structure
of mathematical functions like deep neural networks. To make things simple, we will mainly look at a differentiable function $f$ composed of two differentiable functions $g: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{p}$ and $h: \mathbb{R}^{p} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{m}$, such that $f = h \circ g: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{m}$. The insights gained from this toy example should translate directly to more deeply composed functions $f = g^{(L)} \circ g^{(L-1)} \circ \cdots \circ g^{(1)}$, and even computational graphs with more complex branching.
The chain rule
For a function $f: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{m}$ and a point of linearization $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$, the Jacobian matrix $J_f(\mathbf{x})$ is the $m \times n$ matrix of first-order partial derivatives, whose $(i,j)$-th entry is
\[\big( \Jf \big)_{i,j} = \dfdx{i}{j} \in \sR \, .\]
For a composed function
\[\colorf{f} = \colorh{h} \circ \colorg{g} \, ,\]
the
multivariate chain rule
tells us that we obtain the Jacobian matrix of $f$ by
multiplying
the Jacobian matrices of $h$ and $g$:
\[\Jfc = \Jhc \cdot \Jgc .\]
Figure 1 illustrates this for $n=5$, $m=4$ and $p=3$. We will keep using these dimensions in following illustrations, even though the real benefits of ASD only appear as the dimension grows.
Figure 1: Visualization of the multivariate chain rule for $f = h \circ g$.
AD is matrix-free
We have seen how the chain rule translates the compositional structure of a function into the product structure of its Jacobian matrix. In practice however, there is a problem:
computing intermediate Jacobian matrices is inefficient and often intractable
, especially with a dense matrix format. Examples of dense matrix formats include NumPy’s
ndarray
, PyTorch’s
Tensor
, JAX’s
Array
and Julia’s
Matrix
.

data.title: Understanding Information Architecture
data.author: softwaredoug
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据与信息的管理问题，尤其是在大量使用大语言模型（LLMs）生成文本的情况下，如何有效组织和结构化信息。

不同观点：
• 观点一：[hcarvalhoalves] 认为当前的公司和机构虽然拥有大量数据，但缺乏有效的组织和信息管理能力。随着大语言模型（LLMs）生成大量非结构化文本，这一问题变得更加严重。论据包括数据泛滥的现状以及LLMs生成文本缺乏结构化信息的问题。

• 观点二：隐含反对或补充观点——未直接出现但可推断出，可能有人认为LLMs可以有效帮助组织和结构化信息。这种观点可能基于LLMs在自然语言处理上的进步及其潜在的辅助功能，例如信息分类、摘要生成等。

补充讨论：
• 讨论点一：LLMs生成文本的质量和结构问题。LLMs虽然能生成大量文本，但缺乏内在的结构和组织，导致信息过载。
• 讨论点二：数据管理的需求增加。随着数据量的增长，公司和机构面临如何有效管理和利用这些数据的问题。
• 争议焦点：LLMs在信息组织和管理中的实际效用。一方认为LLMs加重了信息过载和混乱，另一方可能认为LLMs可以通过适当应用帮助解决这些问题。

总结来看，讨论围绕数据管理的挑战和LLMs在这一领域的作用展开，主要争议在于LLMs是加重了信息混乱还是能够帮助解决这一问题。

data.title: WorldGen: Open-source 3D scene generator for Game/VR/XR
data.author: ziyangxie
data.article_summary: WorldGen是一款强大的3D内容生成工具，能够在几秒钟内通过简单的文本提示生成详细的3D场景。它支持文本和图像输入，灵活生成各种场景，并允许360°自由探索。该工具首先生成高分辨率的360度全景图，然后将其转换为完整的3D场景，支持交互式探索。用户可以通过提供的示例和交互演示体验其功能，并访问GitHub仓库开始生成自己的3D场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于生成3D场景工具的功能、实用性和未来发展的不同观点

不同观点：
• **atrus**：认为当前的生成模型缺乏中间文件输出功能，如.blend或Godot项目文件等。这使得在需要对细节（如移动某个物体）进行调整时非常不便，用户可能会陷入不断调整提示或种子的困境。

• **socalgal2**：对工具的期望与实际结果有差距。工具生成的是3D全景图而非完整的3D场景，移动出中心位置后，被遮挡的部分会缺失。期望未来版本能自动填补缺失部分。

• **doshaa**：对AI项目的泛滥感到不满，认为很多项目只是为了理论上的可行性，缺乏实用性。建议加上“AI”标签和警告信息，提醒用户可能出现的性能问题。

• **firtoz**：赞赏不同方法生成世界的尝试，并提到其团队在Greybox上进行的类似实验。他们使用Claude 3.7生成Lua脚本来定义场景，并计划尝试其他方法，如从3D模型生成场景组件。

• **jimmySixDOF**：对工具的整合表示赞赏，并建议将该工具开源，放在HuggingFace空间上。

• **pedalpete**：对工具的发展感到兴奋，并提到自己曾创办过类似的3D场景生成器。认为通过AI生成场景是未来的趋势。

• **whywhywhywhy**：认为工具在当前状态下声称适用于游戏/VR/XR是夸大其词。工具生成的全景图仅适用于固定位置的VR体验，在游戏中可能仅能用于环境地图或非互动背景。

• **pdntspa**：提到工具的输出结果让人联想到Cyberpunk 2077的braindances。

• **Ono-Sendai**：认为工具生成的不是真正的3D，更像是2.5D。

• **ivape**：关注工具对硬件的要求，特别是对Nvidia显卡和所需显存量的疑问。

• 对工具生成内容的实用性存在争议，部分用户认为当前功能有限，期望未来版本能改进。
• 对工具的硬件要求和性能优化也有一定关注，尤其是对显卡和显存的需求。

data.title: LibreLingo – FOSS Alternative to Duolingo
data.author: hyperific
data.article_summary: LibreLingo是一个由Dániel Kántor及多位贡献者创建的社区驱动的语言学习平台。该平台提供多种语言的学习，包括西班牙语、德语、法语、孟加拉语、中古波斯语、巴斯克语、以及针对不同语言背景的拉迪诺语（英语、希伯来语、西班牙语使用者）和针对英语使用者的Houma语。LibreLingo的源代码基于AGPL-3.0许可证，并提供英文的开发文档和工具。平台鼓励社区参与和贡献，以不断扩展语言学习资源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：语言学习方法和工具的比较，特别是对Duolingo等语言学习平台的评价

不同观点：
• **支持Krashen输入假说和直接教学法**：sieve认为Krashen的输入假说和Orberg的直接教学法（如Lingva Latina）是成年人学习语言的有效方式。通过阅读保持上下文的故事，大脑能自动识别语言模式，而无需刻意记忆语法规则。这种方法虽然最终需要超越故事材料，但整体有效。

• **Duolingo的优缺点**：
  - **优点**：pergadad认为Duolingo通过游戏化机制提供了无决策负担的体验，适合入门。_fat_santa和salimmadjd指出Duolingo在词汇学习方面表现出色，可以作为日常动机工具。
  - **缺点**：_fat_santa、anothereng、Tor3、est和jmyeet批评Duolingo过度依赖翻译、句式结构教学不足、内容重复且游戏化过强，可能导致学习效率低下，难以真正掌握语言。jmyeet特别指出其测试机制存在漏洞，可以通过技巧猜对答案而不实际学习。

• **替代工具和方法**：
  - **Anki + 沉浸式学习**：joaohaas推荐Anki结合沉浸式学习，提供具体指南，认为效果更好。
  - **Language Transfer**：pergadad、simonbarker87推荐Language Transfer，认为其比Duolingo更有效。
  - **LibreLingo**：daniel_iversen分享了LibreLingo的开发背景，但未深入评价其效果。

补充讨论：
• **用户体验和技术问题**：
  - zelphirkalt指出LibreLingo在技术实现上存在延迟和界面问题，建议增加加载动画和错误报告功能。
  - mentalgear对LibreLingo的界面设计给予积极评价，但建议改进键盘导航和视觉效果。

• **商业化和市场环境**：
  - hyperific提到Duolingo用AI替代承包商的近期新闻，指出其商业化策略的变化。
  - pergadad批评商业语言学习平台普遍存在锁定用户的现象，缺乏明确的引导路径。

争议焦点：
• **Duolingo的有效性**：一方认为Duolingo作为入门工具和词汇学习器有效，另一方则批评其教学方法浅显，过度依赖游戏化和翻译，无法真正帮助用户掌握语言。

data.title: Creating beautiful charts with JRuby and JFreeChart
data.author: headius
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何使用JRuby和JFreeChart库创建精美的图表。作者在RubyKaigi会议上展示了JRuby的潜力，并指出在CRuby中使用外部库（尤其是C或非Ruby库）的困难，例如Charty库实际上包装了Python的matplotlib。相比之下，JRuby可以通过其Java集成轻松使用JVM库，而无需编写C、Python或JavaScript代码。

文章详细说明了如何通过JRuby调用Java库，特别是JFreeChart库，来生成图表和图像。步骤包括下载jar文件及依赖项，使用`require`加载它们，并直接从Ruby代码中调用Java类。文中还介绍了如何利用`jar-dependencies`工具简化Maven库的管理。通过JRuby，开发者可以方便地构建图表和GUI工具，无需复杂的跨语言绑定。

43850309.article_content:
Creating Beautiful Charts with JRuby and JFreeChart
I recently returned from
RubyKaigi
where I had the opportunity to sit down with members of the Japanese Ruby community and show them a little bit of JRuby. One of the items that came up a few times was the difficulty of utilizing external libraries from Ruby: if it’s a C library, typically you have to either write a C extension or do the extra work of writing up an FFI binding.
If the library is not implemented in C or Ruby, things get even weirder.
One example is the
Charty
library, one of the more popular options for generating beautiful chart graphics on Ruby. But Charty actually wraps a
Python
library called
matplotlib
, and the bindings for CRuby literally load Python into the current process and call it via Ruby C API calls which then make Python C API calls. The horror!
Also recently, a
Reddit Ruby post
demonstrated the use of the QuickChart library, which is implemented in JavaScript… yuck! In this case, the call-out is via process launching to the QuickChart command line, but either way it’s not at really integrated into the Ruby app using it.
Is there a better way? You bet there is: use a JVM-based library from JRuby! This post will show you how to get started with JRuby’s Java integration and a few quick examples of using the JFreeChart library from Ruby code. I promise you won’t have to write a single line of Java, C, Python, or JavaScript.
JFreeChart
The
JFreeChart library
provides an extensive set of chart formats, with a huge array of rendering options and easy integration with either JVM-based GUI toolkits or simple image-file output. Unlike many of the other charting libraries, it also supports live updating of a given chart GUI, making it an excellent choice for desktop monitoring tools.
Building a GUI with JRuby is fun and easy, but for this post we’ll focus on just the chart and image generation parts of the API and how you can use them easily from Ruby.
JRuby’s Java Integration
The magic starts with JRuby’s
Java integration layer
. The simplest way to use a Java library is to basically pretend it’s a Ruby library, with a few tweaks along the way:
Download the library’s jar file and dependencies, or use jar-dependencies (part of JRuby’s standard library) to fetch them for you.
Require the jar file and dependencies manually (a simple
require "myfile.jar"
works in JRuby!) or by using
require_jar
from
jar-dependencies
.
Call the Java classes you’re interested from Ruby as if they were plain old Ruby classes. You can even import them, Java-style, but it’s often not necessary.
Let’s start with a simple example.
Calling into the java.lang.Runtime class
Assuming you’ve installed
JRuby 10
, you can start playing with JVM libraries directly from IRB. Let’s fire it up and make sure we’re running on JRuby.
$ irb
irb(main):001> RUBY_ENGINE
=> "jruby"
irb(main):002>
The JDK comes with a large number of built-in features, of course, and I like to use the
java.lang.Runtime
class for quick demonstrations. It provides methods to query a bit of information about the running JVM and the host operating system. Let’s “import” it into our session and call a few methods.
irb(main):002> rt = java.lang.Runtime.runtime
=> #<Java::JavaLang::Runtime:0x39a87e72>
irb(main):003> rt.available_processors
=> 8
irb(main):004> rt.free_memory
=> 222145360
There’s a few bits of magic here that make it really feel like Ruby:
JRuby defines a few top-level methods for common Java package roots like
java
,
javax
,
org
, and
com
. We use this to reference the Java package
java.lang
here and access the
Runtime
class.
Runtime
defines a static method (similar to a Ruby class or singleton method) called
getRuntime
which gets the singleton instance of
Runtime
for the current JVM process. JRuby turns Java “getter” and “setter” methods into Ruby “attribute accessors”, so you can just call
Runtime.runtime
here.
The Ruby calls to
available_processors
and
free_memory
translate to the Java methods
getAvailableProcessors
and
getFreeMemory
in the same way. The original methods are still callable, but we add aliases for the Ruby-friendly names.
We can accomplish a tremendous amount with the libraries shipped in the JDK, ranging from simple database access to professional desktop GUI development.
If the libraries we want to use are not shipped with the JDK, however, we need to fetch them. It’s always possible to download the library’s “jar” file directly, but then you may also have to hunt down its dependency jars. A better way is to use JRuby’s
jar-dependencies
library.
jar-dependencies
Like Ruby gems get pushed to
rubygems.org
, Java libraries get published as jar files to
Maven
repositories, a global, federated repository of every version of every Java library known to man. In order to make it as easy as possible to use these libraries from JRuby, we’ve built extensive Maven tooling for both Ruby and Java applications.
The simplest way to load a JVM library from Maven into your JRuby app is

data.title: The Art of Managing Skunks
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 本文总结了作者从学术研究转向行业后，参与的两个软件项目的经验和管理心得。这些项目最初都是由2-3人的小型团队起步，逐渐扩展为数十人参与的大型工程。第一个项目是Meta的Delos系统，一个类似于Chubby/ZooKeeper的控制平面存储系统；第二个项目是新的Kafka引擎，可运行于任何分解存储层。作者指出，技术挑战之外，管理这些项目的难度更大，尤其是在激励机制与创新不兼容的情况下。作者提出了几条管理原则：A. 非编码的架构师不可参与设计；B. 团队成员无个人“所有权”，共担责任；C. 发挥个人长处而非弥补短处；D. 对外沟通必须精确、高质量并经过审查。这些原则旨在帮助其他工程师和管理人员有效管理创新项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工程团队管理与技术债务的平衡

不同观点：
• PaulRobinson：认为文章中的建议总体不错，但需要在发挥个人优势和个人成长之间找到平衡。他指出，团队需要定期进行成长训练，以保持长期有效性。他还提到，尽管团队成员需要共同承担责任，但通过讨论明确工作所有权有助于提高可见性和速度。
• hoistbypetard：引用了Fred Brooks的观点，指出几乎所有软件项目从第一天起就落后于计划。通过个人经验，强调了接受这一现实的必要性，并提到Fred Brooks本人也认同这一看法。
• freedomben：对文章中关于逐步增加团队负荷的观点持保留态度。他认为，这种方式可能导致技术债务，并在未来增加开发和维护成本。他主张在管理项目时应追求平衡，而不是一味追求快速交付，并认为这是现代软件质量低下的原因之一。
• antman：对文章中的理想化场景持怀疑态度。他认为假设一个小团队、没有外部依赖、管理层不干预等条件是不现实的，并暗示这种方法难以在复杂项目中实施。

补充讨论：
• aaroninsf：对文章作者的才华表示赞赏，但质疑作者为何选择为一家在社会、政治和文化方面有负面影响的公司工作，批评了该公司以利润为唯一导向的行为。

争议的焦点：
• 主要集中在团队管理中如何平衡短期交付压力与长期技术健康，特别是技术债务的累积和其对未来维护的影响。不同的评论者根据自身经验提出了对文章建议的适用性和现实性的不同看法。

43862774.article_content:
Since moving from academic research to industry in 2017, Iâve worked on two software projects. Each one started as a small, clean-slate
1
skunkworks effort involving 2-3 people and gradually expanded to a large, conventional software engineering effort with dozens of engineers. The first of these (from 2017 to 2021) was
Delos
at Meta, a Chubby/ZooKeeper/etcd-like control plane storage system. The second was a new Kafka engine (from 2022 to 2024) that can run on any disaggregated storage layer (and powers the Confluent Freight product, where S3 is used as that storage layer). Nearly every system at Meta depends in some way on Delos as of 2025 (e.g., this
article
describes an example dependency chain); Confluent Freight just became
generally available
and time will tell if it succeeds commercially, though early results are promising.
While these systems were technically difficult to build and operate (particularly given their critical roles in the stacks of the respective companies), I found that much of the challenge lay in the management of these projects. Even the most innovative companies on the planet have incentive structures (for line managers and engineers) that are incompatible with clean-slate skunkworks innovation. In my discussions with various managers over the last few years, I found myself converging on a set of key principles, which I outline in this article. I hope these rules are helpful for other engineers and managers looking to define a shared set of principles for their own skunkworks projects.
Some caveats: I am an engineer, not a manager, and have never managed anything in my life beyond a handful of interns and graduate students; this is just my wish-list as a technical project lead / architect for what I need from managers. These rules may be highly specific to building new storage services at large companies. At some point, the project has to exit skunkworks mode and these rules cease to apply. My sample size is N=2 and itâs difficult to establish that these rules are causally related (or even just correlated) to project success.
A. No non-coding architects:
If you want to participate in designing the system, you have to write code. (Note that itâs okay to not code if you are bringing some particular expertise to the table: e.g., if you are a world-class erasure coding theorist. It might also be okay if you are a world-class ops specialist, though in my experience most such people are very comfortable with code). If thereâs anyone on the team whose only job is to delegate work to other people, something has gone extremely wrong.
B. No individual âownershipâ:
Everyone is responsible for everything. If the boat sinks, everyone sinks with it; thereâs no way to win or lose independently. We want people accelerating and enabling each other to expand the pie, not competing with each other on a fixed pie. We want zero tolerance for self-promoting activity: it is the job of the manager and the TLs to make sure that people are rewarded fairly based on what they actually did. The best managers of such teams tell them to run as fast as possible and get the job done; and take the burden of justifying ratings completely off the engineers. If the need to safeguard an engineerâs rating begins to shape the projectâs priorities, something has gone extremely wrong.
C. Operate on strengths, not weaknesses:
We want each person to focus on what they are truly good at; rather than what they are weakest at. The latter often happens in a big company setup when engineers want to get promoted; and managers tell them to focus on the areas that are holding them back. If engineers ask managers what will get them promoted, the answer has to be ârun as fast as you can and make the team shipâ. If that person cannot get objectively promoted under those circumstances, something has gone extremely wrong: the project is not impactful enough to warrant a skunkworks approach; or the person should not be on this project (e.g., maybe their skillset is not needed on the project, or they are not good enough in their assumed area of expertise, etc.).
D. Formal communication (exposed outside the team) has to be extremely precise, high-quality, and reviewed:
To paraphrase Jeff Bezos, we want âcrisp documents and messy meetingsâ. Different constituencies need different types of messaging: some may need to know about technically impressive details; others may want to know about business impact; some may need to know whatâs happening next month and others may need to know whatâs happening in 3 years. Writing a single document with that kind of versatility takes months even for experienced writers. Everything the team says publicly impacts its reputation and credibility; and constrains its actions in the future. Note that this is not at odds with transparency: informal communication should happen at all levels with the utmost transparency, since itâs typically easy to convey nuance and context when

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于电力系统中使用三相交流和直流混合传输的简化与效率问题

不同观点：
• deepsun认为，通过节省电线来简化系统是有价值的，但作为建造者可能会为了节省成本而选择更复杂的系统。他认为多加电线可以简化系统，但成本可能会增加。
• bill3478对该系统的实际应用场景提出质疑，指出三相低压交流加上直流的应用场景有限，主要在工业负载和控制中使用。他还对直流部分的传输效率表示怀疑，认为可能需要昂贵的降压转换器。
• analog31提出一个有趣的类比，将该系统与麦克风幻象供电进行比较，指出在同一对电线上传输电力和信号的可能性。
• SigmundA认为中性线共享并没有太大意义，因为导体尺寸仍然需要增加。他详细介绍了现代混合逆变器的技术，如高频设计和高电压直流（HVDC）总线，并预测未来可能会有更多的HVDC应用，如电动汽车充电和简化的电池系统。他同时承认传统交流配电的简单性和可靠性难以超越。
• 486sx33对系统的复杂性提出直接批评，认为增加一个额外的故障点是不必要的，暗示这样的系统可能不够可靠。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了未来电力系统中HVDC的潜力，特别是在太阳能和电动汽车充电方面的应用。
• 对现有技术如高频变压器的介绍，提供了关于当前和未来技术趋势的背景信息。
• 争议的焦点主要在于系统的简化与复杂性、成本与效率之间的平衡，以及新技术在实际应用中的可行性和可靠性。

data.title: DECtalk Archive
data.author: classichasclass
data.article_summary: DECtalk是1984年由Digital Equipment Corporation（DEC）推出的语音合成器，基于丹尼斯·克拉特（Dennis Klatt）在20世纪60-70年代的研究，特别是他开发的Klattalk系统。克拉特创建了包括"Perfect Paul"在内的多种语音模型。DEC于1983年获得Klattalk的独家授权，并于1984年发布首款硬件产品DECtalk DTC-01，售价4000美元。后续版本包括1992年的DECtalk PC（ISA卡）和1994年的DECtalk Express（外接设备），均支持语音合成。1994年，DEC还推出了Windows NT上的软件版本DECtalk，并提供SDK。DECtalk的声音尤其以其独特的"Perfect Paul"语音而闻名。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DECtalk及其相关技术（包括历史、应用和比较）

不同观点：
• HarHarVeryFunny：介绍了DECtalk（DTC-01）的技术原理和历史背景，强调其基于共振峰的语音合成方式。他认为这种合成方式使其既能说话也能唱歌，尽管声音人工化，但在加速播放时非常清晰，特别适合盲人用户使用。他还提到后来的语音合成器更多是基于拼接录音，声音更自然但功能受限。
• neilv：分享了自己在学校项目中使用DECtalk的经历，通过手动调整让DECtalk的输出更具表现力，比如对《葛底斯堡演讲》片段的注释和调试。这表明通过精细调整，DECtalk可以产生更具感染力的语音输出。
• larusso：提到Apple的AirPods在多语言支持上的问题，特别是Siri在读德语和英语消息时的表现不一致，有时会使用类似DECtalk的计算机声音，且这种切换似乎是随机的，显示出现代语音技术在多语言处理上的局限性。
• hcarvalhoalves：询问DECtalk是否是史蒂芬·霍金使用过的技术，暗示DECtalk在历史上的重要性和广泛应用。
• ValveFan6969：提到更早的Commodore 64 SAM技术，并提供了在线JavaScript版本链接，显示出DECtalk并非唯一的早期语音合成技术。
• DonHopkins：分享了Peter Langston使用DECtalk进行音乐生成的历史和相关资源，包括经典的Eedie & Eddie音乐作品和相关技术论文，展示了DECtalk在艺术创作中的应用。

补充讨论：
• DECtalk的技术原理和应用场景：包括其基于共振峰的语音合成方式、在盲人用户中的应用、以及其既能说话又能唱歌的能力。
• DECtalk的历史地位：通过提到史蒂芬·霍金和Peter Langston等著名用户，显示其在历史上的重要性。
• 现代语音技术的局限性：如Siri在多语言支持上的问题，与DECtalk形成对比。
• 早期语音合成技术的比较：如Commodore 64 SAM与DECtalk的比较，显示不同技术的发展路径。

争议焦点：
• 现代语音技术在多语言处理上的表现不如人意，与DECtalk等早期技术相比，其智能性和一致性受到质疑。

What is DECtalk
DECtalk is a speech synthesizer, originally released as a hardware module in 1984 by Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC).
DECtalk's origins
The DECtalk technology is based on the work of Dennis Klatt, who was a pioneer in speech synthesis throughout the 1960s and 1970s. He developed the phoneme-to-speech part of a system known as MITalk, a project developed at MIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), using recordings of his own voice to build a functioning voice model, later to be known as Perfect Paul. Perfect Paul would end up being a model emulating how Klatt talked in his younger days. In 1982, Klatt developed his own speech system nown as Klattalk, which added other voices to give a much wider selection, most of which were modelled after his family. This included Beautiful Betty, modelled after Klatt's wife, and a child voice, Kit the Kid, modelled after his daughter. In 1983, DEC bought an exclusive license to Klattalk to use it in their own products, the first of which was released in 1984 under the name "DECtalk".
DECtalk editions
Digital Equipment Corporation and others (1984-2000)
When DEC licensed the system and released it as DECtalk, they continued to collaborate with Klatt on the development, until his dead in 1988, whereafter DEC continued development until the late 90s, both as hardware, and later software products. Hardware products included, but were not limited to:
DECtalk DTC-01: This was the original 1984 model, which was a standalone unit, mainly used in call centers to make and receive calls. At $4000, it was way to expensive to be used for much else. It originally used DECtalk version 1.8, and was later upgraded to version 2.0, which added two new voices, Doctor Dennis and Whispering Wendy. The DECtalk DTC-01 has now been made available as a
MAME emulator
, which can be used to type in text and have it read by either DECtalk 1.8 or 2.0.

DECtalk PC and PC2 (DTC-07): This was an ISA card released in 1992, dessigned to fit directly into an IBM or compatible computer running DOS, and provide speech synthesis to any program on the computer, including screen readers for the blind and visually impaired. The DECtalk PC was released with DECtalk version 4.0, but was later upgrade up through the 4.x line, with the last version from DEC being version 4.2CD, which is generally accepted among DECtalk enthusiasts to be the best sounding version of DECtalk in existence. The DECtalk PC, like the DTC-01, has now been made available in a
MAME emulator

DECtalk Express (DTC-08): This was a small, external speech synthesizer released in 1994. The unit connected to a computer through an RS232 serial port, and could provide speech synthesis to any program on the computer able to send text to a serial port, through it's own build-in speaker. It's primary intended use was to provide speech to screen readers for the blind and visually impaired, and the JAWS for Windows screen reader still provides compatibility for the DECtalk Express to this day. The DECtalk Express was released with DECtalk version 4.2, and the last version from DEC for the DECtalk Express was version 4.2CD, just like the DECtalk PC.

DECtalk software was available as a SDK for developers, though it could be demonstrated for free through a demo program, which allowed a user to type in text and have it read aloud by DECtalk. The voice sounded mostly similar to the DECtalk hardware products, though it had a few differences in the sound and how it behaved, some of which related to the singing.

data.title: C++26: more constexpr in the standard library
data.author: npalli
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了C++26中将成为constexpr的几个标准库特性。首先提到P2562R1提案，建议使与稳定排序相关的算法（如`std::stable_sort`、`std::stable_partition`等）可在常量表达式中使用，这得益于constexpr容器的引入。接着讨论P1383R2提案，旨在使`<cmath>`和`<complex>`中的函数在常量表达式中可用，同时接受浮点计算结果的某些差异。然后是P3074R7提案，解决了实现constexpr友好的unions时遇到的问题，通过最小化用户体验的改变来实现。最后，P3372R2提案旨在使几乎所有容器和适配器成为constexpr，除了`std::hive`和需要自定义哈希功能的无序容器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C++的编译时常量计算及其复杂性，以及标准委员会在解决语言问题上的优先级

不同观点：
• WalterBright认为D语言在2007年就已经实现了编译时的常量函数计算，而无需对语法进行更改，只是增强了常量折叠以处理函数调用。他不理解为什么在C++中这个问题如此复杂。
• gitroom表示虽然经常看到不断的更新，但感觉一些主要的痛点问题长期未得到解决，有时觉得标准在追逐错误的问题。
• nokeya讽刺地说，这项功能即使在所有主要编译器都支持的情况下，也要到2040年左右才能在实际中看到。
• kubav027基于自己的职业经历认为，某些功能（如constexpr排序）非常小众，不应成为C++标准的一部分。
• brooke2k对"constexpr排序"表示担忧，认为这可能会引发编译时的问题。
• dvratil则认为委员会没有优先解决语言和标准库中的更大问题，比如用简短的代码实现异步网络请求，而是在处理一些相对次要的技术细节。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是C++标准委员会的优先级问题，一些开发者认为委员会在解决小问题的同时，忽略了语言和库中更大的、更实际的问题。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对constexpr功能（如排序）的实用性存在质疑，部分开发者认为这些功能过于小众，不应成为标准的一部分。
• 还有对C++功能实现的时间进度表示不满，认为新功能的实际可用性被严重延迟。

43861669.article_content:
Last week, we discussed
language features that are becoming
constexpr
in C++26
. Today, let’s turn our attention to the standard library features that will soon be usable at compile time. One topic is missing: exceptions. As they need both core language and library changes, I thought they deserved their own post.
P2562R1
:
constexpr
stable sorting
This paper proposes making
std::stable_sort
,
std::stable_partition
,
std::inplace_merge
, and their
ranges
counterparts usable in constant expressions. While many algorithms have become
constexpr
over the years, this family related to stable sorting had remained exceptions — until now.
The recent introduction of
constexpr
containers gives extra motivation for this proposal. If you can construct a container at compile time, it’s only natural to want to sort it there, too. More importantly, a
constexpr std::vector
can now support efficient, stable sorting algorithms.
A key question is whether the algorithm can meet its computational complexity requirements under the constraints of constant evaluation. Fortunately,
std::is_constant_evaluated()
provides an escape hatch for implementations. For deeper details, check out the
proposal
itself.
P1383R2
: More
constexpr
for
<cmath>
and
<complex>
While
P0533
made many
<cmath>
and
<cstdlib>
functions
constexpr
-friendly in C++23, it only addressed functions with trivial behavior — those no more complex than the basic arithmetic operators.
Floating-point computations can yield different results depending on compiler settings, optimization levels, and hardware platforms. For instance, calculating
std::sin(1e100)
may produce varying outcomes due to the intricacies of floating-point arithmetic at such scales. The paper discusses these challenges and suggests that some variability in results is acceptable, given the nature of floating-point computations.
The proposal
accepts the need for a balance between strict determinism and practical flexibility. It suggests that while some functions should produce consistent results across platforms, others may inherently allow for some variability.
P3074R7
: trivial
union
s (was
std::uninitialized<T>
)
To implement static, in-place,
constexpr
-friendly containers like non-allocating vectors, you often need uninitialized storage — typically via
union
s. However, default behavior for special members of unions has been limiting: if not all alternatives are trivial, the special member is deleted. This presents a problem for
constexpr
code where a no-op destructor isn’t quite the same as a trivial one.
The road to solving this wasn’t short:
P3074R7
went through seven revisions and considered five possible solutions—including library-based approaches, new annotations, and even a new union type. Ultimately, the committee decided to just
make it work
with minimal changes to the user experience.
But how?
For unions, the default constructor - if there is no default member initializer - is always going to be trivial. If the first alternative is an implicit-lifetime time, it begins its life-time and becomes the active member.
The defaulted destructor is deleted if either the union has a user-provided default constructor or there exists a variant alternative that has a default member initializer and that member’s destructor is either deleted or inaccessible. Otherwise, the destructor is trivial.

P3372R2
:
constexpr
containers and adaptors
Hana Dusíková authored
a massive proposal
that boils down to a simple goal: make (almost) all containers and adaptors
constexpr
.
Up until now, only a handful of them were
constexpr
-friendly (
std::vector
,
std::span
,
std::mdspan
,
std::basic_string
and
std::basic_string_view
). From now on, the situation will be flipped. Almost everything will be
constexpr
-friendly. There is one exception and one constraint:
std::hive
is not included, because it doesn’t have a stable wording yet
if you want to use unordered containers at compile-time, you must provide your own hashing facility, because
std::hash
cannot be made
constexpr
-friendly due to its requirements. Its result is guaranteed to be consistent only with the duration of the program.
Happy days!

data.title: Oxide’s compensation model: how is it going?
data.author: steveklabnik
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Oxide公司四年前推出的薪酬模式及其成效。当时公司规模小，招聘困难，为吸引更多人才，他们决定公开透明的薪酬制度，所有员工薪资统一且透明，这一做法引发了广泛关注。文章更新提到，2025年该薪酬已增至207,264美元，并且为某些销售岗位引入了浮动薪酬。尽管外界担忧这种模式会导致员工懈怠，但实际情况相反，员工非常重视个人表现和招聘工作。该模式鼓励员工专注于自身贡献，并认真对待招聘，因为所有员工都是平等的“ peers”，对新同事的期望很高。此外，该模式也强调了不同岗位的重要性，尤其是在传统上被低估的支持角色。总体来看，该薪酬模式运行良好，帮助公司吸引了志同道合的人才并推动了公司发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Oxide公司独特的管理结构和薪酬模式，及其在现实中的可行性和可持续性。

不同观点：
• [abxyz] 认为Oxide的模式在依赖投资资金时显得空洞，对该模式能否在需要自负盈亏时持续表示怀疑。特别指出支持岗位的薪酬过高，且在压力下这些岗位可能最先受到挤压。
• [michaelt] 对一些人贬低支持岗位的价值感到不满，认为这是对接近客户的角色的贬低。建议通过外包来避免支付高薪给某些岗位。
• [wavemode] 对Oxide消除中层管理的努力表示赞赏，认为虽然会面临挑战，但传统企业结构也存在大量浪费，新的尝试值得鼓励。
• [boulos] 讨论了股权与现金补偿的关系，认为Oxide的薪酬模式是一个合理的选择，并指出股权授予自然会有变化。
• [whazor] 分享了自己追求平等薪酬策略的经验，指出100%统一薪酬可能导致忽视培养初级工程师的责任。
• [jamietanna] 对Oxide的透明薪酬模式表示赞赏，并分享了自己的公开薪酬链接以示支持。
• [VladVladikoff] 对Oxide的产品和销售模式感到困惑，指出其网站不清晰，难以理解具体产品和价格。
• [endianswap] 希望Oxide对销售岗位的例外情况做出更多解释，认为这可能削弱其他主张的说服力。
• [cashsterling] 对Oxide的招聘流程表示了一定的不满，但对其补偿模式和公司文化表示赞赏。
• [carstenhag] 担心随着时间推移，表现不佳的员工也会获得相同薪酬，这可能导致不公平感，并对团队动力产生负面影响。
• [cobertos] 提出即使消除了金钱的稀缺性，时间和知识产权可能成为新的稀缺资源，仍可能导致不良激励。
• [serhack_] 对Oxide的云产品如何购买和保证数据本地化提出了具体问题，表示对客户需求的关注。
• [latchkey] 希望看到Oxide的收入模式如何运作，对其目前的产品演示和销售转化表示好奇。

补充讨论：
• Oxide的创新管理和薪酬模式引发了关于支持岗位价值、销售岗位例外、股权与现金补偿、以及公司未来可持续性的广泛讨论。
• 一些评论者对Oxide的透明和创新表示赞赏，而另一些则对其现实可行性、公平性和网站清晰度提出了质疑。
• 网站设计和产品销售模式的清晰度也是评论中提到的值得注意的问题。

43862487.article_content:
1 May 2025
Oxideâs Compensation Model: How is it Going?
Bryan Cantrill
CTO
How it started
Four years ago, we were struggling to hire. Our team was small (~23
employees), and we knew that we needed many more people to execute on our
audacious vision
.  While we had
had success hiring in our personal networks, those networks now felt tapped;
we needed to get further afield.  As is our wont, we got together as a team
and brainstormed: how could we get a bigger and broader applicant pool?  One
of our engineers, Sean, shared some personal experience: that
Oxide’s principles and values
were very
personally important to him — but that when he explained them to people
unfamiliar with the company, they were (understandably?) dismissed as
corporate claptrap.  Sean had found, however, that there was one surefire way
to cut through the skepticism:  to explain our approach to compensation.
Maybe, Sean wondered, we should talk about it publicly?
"I could certainly write a blog entry explaining it," I offered.  At this
suggestion, the team practically lunged with enthusiasm: the reaction was so
uniformly positive that I have to assume that everyone was sick of explaining
this most idiosyncratic aspect of Oxide to friends and family.  So what was
the big deal about our compensation?  Well, as a I wrote in the resulting
piece,
Compensation
as a Reflection of Values
, our compensation is not merely transparent, but
uniform.  The piece — unsurprisingly, given the evergreen hot topic that is
compensation — got a ton of attention.  While some of that attention was
negative (despite the piece trying to frontrun every HN hater!), much of it was
positive — and everyone seemed to be at least intrigued.
And in terms of its initial purpose, the piece succeeded beyond our wildest
imagination: it brought a surge of new folks interested in the company.  Best
of all, the people new to Oxide were interested for all of the right reasons:
not the compensation
per se
, but for the values that the compensation
represents.  The deeper they dug, the more they found to like — and many who
learned about Oxide for the first time through that blog entry we now count as
long-time, cherished colleagues.
That blog entry was a long time ago now, and today we have ~75 employees
(and a
shipping product
!);
how is our compensation model working out for us?
How itâs going
Before we get into our deeper findings, two updates that are so important that
we have updated the blog entry itself.  First, the dollar figure itself
continues to increase over time (as of this writing in 2025, $207,264);
things definitely haven’t gotten (and aren’t
getting!) any cheaper.  And second, we
did
introduce variable compensation for
some sales roles.  Yes, those roles can make more than the rest of us — but
they can also make less, too.  And, importantly:  if/when those folks are
making more than the rest of us, it’s because they’re selling a lot — a
result that can be celebrated by everyone!
Those critical updates out of the way, how is it working?  There have been a
lot of surprises along the way, mostly (all?) of the positive variety.  A
couple of things that we have learned:
People take their own performance really seriously.
When some outsiders
hear about our compensation model, they insist that it can’t possibly work
because "everyone will slack off." I have come to find this concern to be more
revealing of the person making the objection than of our model, as our
experience has been in fact the opposite: in my one-on-one conversations with
team members, a frequent subject of conversation is people who are concerned
that they aren’t doing enough (or that they aren’t doing the right thing, or
that their work is progressing slower than they would like).  I find my job is
often to help quiet this inner critic while at the same time stoking what I

43862487.article_summary: 本文讨论了Oxide公司四年前推出的薪酬模式及其成效。当时公司规模小，招聘困难，为吸引更多人才，他们决定公开透明的薪酬制度，所有员工薪资统一且透明，这一做法引发了广泛关注。文章更新提到，2025年该薪酬已增至207,264美元，并且为某些销售岗位引入了浮动薪酬。尽管外界担忧这种模式会导致员工懈怠，但实际情况相反，员工非常重视个人表现和招聘工作。该模式鼓励员工专注于自身贡献，并认真对待招聘，因为所有员工都是平等的“ peers”，对新同事的期望很高。此外，该模式也强调了不同岗位的重要性，尤其是在传统上被低估的支持角色。总体来看，该薪酬模式运行良好，帮助公司吸引了志同道合的人才并推动了公司发展。

data.article_summary: 《Robot Unlock》是一款由Adrian Toncean开发和发布的开放式解谜游戏，计划于2025年5月1日发布。游戏包含75个以上的关卡，玩家需在有限空间内使用少量指令解决 puzzles，并可以优化解决方案在速度、指令或空间方面的表现。游戏支持多线程操作、设置断点以及逐步调试，并允许玩家创建和分享自定义关卡，同时解决其他社区玩家设计的关卡。玩家还可以比较各自解决方案的排名。系统要求包括64位处理器和操作系统，推荐使用Windows 11及至少4GB内存。目前无用户评价。游戏在发行首周提供9折优惠，价格为8.99美元。

data.title: The cat that wouldn't die
data.author: Hooke
data.article_summary:
1935年，奥地利物理学家埃尔温·薛定谔发表了一篇对新兴量子力学理论的批评性评论，其中他以半开玩笑的方式提出了著名的“薛定谔的猫”思想实验。实验描述了一只猫被关在装有放射性物质和毒气装置的钢箱中，根据量子力学的波函数理论，猫在一个小时后会处于活与死的叠加状态，直到有人打开箱子观察。

薛定谔通过这个实验旨在揭示量子力学中波函数描述的怪异特性：微观粒子在未被观察时可以同时处于多种状态（叠加态），但宏观物体如猫似乎不应如此。实验的核心问题在于，量子力学的怪异现象究竟何时停止？猫究竟是死是活？

这个思想实验后来成为量子力学中讨论测量问题和叠加态的经典比喻，并在流行文化中广泛传播。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：薛定谔的猫思想实验及其在量子力学中的解释

不同观点：
• [cadamsdotcom] 认为宇宙是“懒惰计算”的，即所有事件和结果都只是概率，直到需要结果时才会被“解析”。在薛定谔猫的实验中，盒子内部的系统是孤立的，猫和放射性粒子在内部系统中会有明确的状态（生或死），但从外部观察时，盒子内的结果可以保持概率状态，无需“解析”。这种观点强调宇宙中没有绝对的真理或事件序列，只有在我们观察范围内近似的真理和事件。

• [nyeah] 不同意上述观点，认为在实际情况下，如果有一个真正的猫和金属盒子，并不会产生所谓的“叠加态”。只有在我们完全无法得知发生了什么的情况下，叠加态才会出现，而不是因为我们还没选择去“摇盒子”。

• [ztetranz] 以幽默的方式简化了讨论，指出“Sean Carroll的猫”要么醒着要么睡着，意在暗示有关量子叠加态的讨论可能被过度复杂化。

• [Nevermark] 强调量子力学的数学公式中并没有描述“塌缩”的方程，所谓的塌缩只是表象。实际上，场方程已经解释了为何我们会感知到塌缩。该观点认为量子塌缩并不真实存在，只是我们感知上的一种现象，所有的现象都可以通过场方程来解释，且有实验和量子计算机等系统证实这些方程。

补充讨论：
• [andrewstuart] 关注实验伦理问题，询问是否有不伤害动物的薛定谔猫实验方法。

• [asdsadasdasd123] 以讽刺的口吻评论，试图用类比来证明某种观点的荒谬性，但这些类比却被普遍接受为现实，这本身就很滑稽。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于量子叠加态和塌缩的本质问题。一部分人认为叠加态是宇宙懒惰计算的结果，而另一部分人则认为实际情况下并不会出现这种叠加态，且所谓的塌缩只是感知上的现象，实际并不存在。

In 1935, the Austrian physicist Erwin Schrödinger published a rather critical three-part review of what he called the ‘present situation’ in the relatively new theory of quantum mechanics. For the most part, Schrödinger’s review, written in German, is dry and technical, and not the kind of thing that would detain anyone outside the narrow academic world of quantum physics. But in one short paragraph, written with his tongue firmly in his cheek, he gave flight to a fancy that,
90 years
later, continues to resonate in popular culture. The paragraph concerned Schrödinger’s eponymous cat. How did an obscure argument about a mathematically complex and rather baffling theory of physics become embedded in public consciousness as an extraordinary exploration of the human psyche? This essay tells the story.
Here’s what Schrödinger wrote (in the English translation by John D Trimmer):
One can even set up quite ridiculous cases. A cat is penned up in a steel chamber, along with the following diabolical device (which must be secured against direct interference from the cat): in a Geiger counter there is a tiny bit of radioactive substance,
so
small that
perhaps
in the course of one hour one of the [radioactive] atoms decays, but also, with equal probability, perhaps none; if it happens, the counter tube discharges and through a relay releases a hammer which shatters a small flask of hydrocyanic acid. If one has left this entire system to itself for an hour, one would say that the cat still lives
if
meanwhile no atom has decayed. The first atomic decay would have poisoned it. The [quantum wavefunction] of the entire system would express this by having in it the living and dead cat (pardon the expression) mixed or smeared out in equal parts.
Although this was only a ‘thought’ experiment, the paradox of Schrödinger’s cat was destined to join Pavlov’s dog in science’s bestiary of the bizarre.
T
o understand the point Schrödinger was making, we need to do a little unpacking. The nature of Schrödinger’s ‘diabolical device’ is not actually important to his argument. Its purpose is simply to
amplify
an atomic-scale event – the decay of a radioactive atom – and bring it up to the more familiar scale of a living cat, trapped inside a steel box. The theory that describes objects and events taking place at the scale of atoms and subatomic particles like electrons is quantum mechanics. But in this theory, atoms and subatomic particles are described not as tiny, self-contained objects moving through space. They are instead described in terms of quantum
wavefunctions
, which capture an utterly weird aspect of their observed behaviour. Under certain circumstances, these particles may also behave like
waves
.
These contrasting behaviours could not be starker, or more seemingly incompatible. Particles have mass. By their nature, they are ‘here’: they are localised in space and remain localised as they move from here to there. Throw many particles into a small space and, like marbles, they will collide, bouncing off each other in different directions. Waves, on the other hand, are spread out through space – they are ‘non-local’. Squeeze them through a narrow slit and, like waves in the sea passing through a gap in a harbour wall, they will spread out beyond. Physicists call this diffraction. Push a bunch of different waves together and they will merge to form what physicists call a
superposition
. The peaks and troughs of all the different waves add together. Where peak meets peak, the result is a larger peak. Where trough meets trough, the result is a deeper trough. Where peak meets trough, they are both reduced and, if they happened to be of equal height and depth, they will completely cancel each other out. Physicists call this interference.
By 1935, the mathematical formulation of quantum mechanics was relatively mature, and acknowledged by most physicists as complete.
But the theory does not say where all the quantum weirdness is supposed to stop.
When applied to the radioactive atom, quantum theory says that, after an hour, the wavefunction of the atom is represented as an equal mix – a superposition – of decayed and undecayed atoms.
So, is the cat dead or alive? We have no way of knowing until we lift the lid of the box, and look
We could choose to stop there, but we know that the interaction between the atom and the diabolical device should also be described by quantum mechanics, at least in its early stages. If we choose to take the theory literally, then extending its equations to include the entire device means that the wavefunction evolves into a superposition of decayed atom and triggered device, and undecayed atom and untriggered device. In his review, Schrödinger coined the term ‘entanglement’ to describe this situation. The radioactive atom becomes entangled with the device.

1935年，奥地利物理学家埃尔温·薛定谔发表了一篇对新兴量子力学理论的批评性评论，其中他以半开玩笑的方式提出了著名的“薛定谔的猫”思想实验。实验描述了一只猫被关在装有放射性物质和毒气装置的钢箱中，根据量子力学的波函数理论，猫在一个小时后会处于活与死的叠加状态，直到有人打开箱子观察。

薛定谔通过这个实验旨在揭示量子力学中波函数描述的怪异特性：微观粒子在未被观察时可以同时处于多种状态（叠加态），但宏观物体如猫似乎不应如此。实验的核心问题在于，量子力学的怪异现象究竟何时停止？猫究竟是死是活？

这个思想实验后来成为量子力学中讨论测量问题和叠加态的经典比喻，并在流行文化中广泛传播。

data.title: New Study: Waymo is reducing serious crashes and making streets safer
data.author: prossercj
data.article_summary: Waymo的最新研究显示，其自动驾驶系统（Waymo Driver）在减少严重交通事故和保护弱势道路使用者（如行人、骑自行车者）方面取得显著进展。研究对比了Waymo Driver与人类驾驶员在5670万英里驾驶数据中的表现，发现Waymo在以下方面有明显改善：与弱势道路使用者的碰撞减少了92%（行人）、82%（骑自行车者）和82%（摩托车手）；交叉路口的伤人事故减少了96%；严重受伤事故减少了85%。这些结果表明，Waymo Driver有助于实现“零交通死亡”的愿景，并在提升道路安全方面发挥关键作用。

43861828.article_content:
Back to all posts
The path to Vision Zero requires reducing severe crashes and improving the safety of those most at risk. Our
latest research paper
shows that the Waymo Driver is making significant strides in both areas. By reducing the most dangerous crashes and providing better protection for pedestrians, cyclists, and other vulnerable road users, Waymo is making streets safer in cities where it operates.
The paper, accepted to be published in the Traffic Injury Prevention Journal, expands on our
Safety Impact Hub
research, providing a deeper analysis of Waymo’s performance across 11 different crash types compared to human drivers. It also offers new insights into Waymo’s positive impact on serious injury crash rates.
Types of crashes used for the Waymo Driver and human benchmark comparisons
The research finds that, compared to human benchmarks over 56.7 million miles and regardless of who was at fault, the Waymo Driver had:
Safer interactions with vulnerable road users (VRUs)
with
substantial reductions in crashes involving injuries among pedestrians (92% reduction), cyclists (82% reduction), and motorcyclists (82% reduction).
96% fewer injury-involving intersection crashes
, which, according to NHTSA, are a leading cause of severe road harm for human drivers. This reduction can be largely attributed to the Waymo Driver’s ability to detect and appropriately respond to vehicles running a red light.
85% fewer crashes with suspected serious or worse injuries
. Building on our previous research, which demonstrated Waymo’s significant reductions across all injuries combined, the new study provides early evidence for similar benefits in serious injuries alone. The results are statistically significant but because serious injury cases are, fortunately, rare, they’re based on a small number of events. We will continue to monitor outcomes and gain greater confidence as we accumulate more miles.
These findings add to the growing body of data that the Waymo Driver is reducing the most dangerous crash types, contributing to safer roadways, and pushing forward a vision of zero traffic deaths and serious injuries on our roads. While this particular research did not account for crash contribution, a previous
study
led by the insurance company Swiss Re demonstrated that the Waymo Driver’s positive impact is even more significant when contribution is taken into account.
“It’s exciting to see the real positive impact that Waymo is making on the streets of America as we continue to expand,”
said Mauricio Peña, Waymo’s Chief Safety Officer.
“This research reinforces the growing evidence that the Waymo Driver is playing a crucial role in reducing serious crashes and protecting all road users.”
“It’s encouraging to see real-world data showing Waymo outperforming human drivers when it comes to safety. Fewer crashes and fewer injuries — especially for people walking and biking — is exactly the kind of progress we want to see from autonomous vehicles,” — said
Jonathan Adkins, Chief Executive Officer at Governors Highway Safety Association.
As Waymo increases in scale, we look forward to strengthening our safety data, assessing the long-term impact on road safety, and helping to advance conversations amongst researchers, policymakers, and safety groups.
We look forward to continuing this conversation and working toward a future where serious traffic injuries, one of the biggest causes of death in the U.S, are dramatically reduced. For those interested in a deeper dive into the data and methodology, we encourage you to explore the
full study
, and our rolling
safety data hub
.

data.title: Making of Monkeys.zip
data.author: yathern
data.article_summary:
《Monkeys.zip》项目上线一个月，已收集超过11,000只“猴子”，生成了超过60亿个单词，完成了莎士比亚作品中75%以上的词汇，最近更完成了所有四字母单词。项目技术栈包括Supabase（后端和数据库）、LitHTML（前端库）、Three.js（3D库）和Astro（博客）。项目模拟架构通过四个主要步骤实现：  
1. **Ticks**：每15秒生成一个新Tick，简单且可靠。  
2. **generateTickText**：根据种子生成随机文本，存储在存储桶中以增加透明度。  
3. **processTick**：分析文本，更新数据库中的相关表格。  
4. **Archive**：定期归档旧数据以提升读取速度。  

项目还包括将猴子网格划分为64x64块，并使用Redis缓存以应对高流量。尽管项目已进入优化阶段，但仍有机会进一步提升性能。

不同观点：
• 正面观点1：部分用户认为该项目有趣且具有实验性，能够引发对随机生成内容和创造力之间关系的思考。有用户指出，项目通过模拟猴子随机打字的行为，巧妙地致敬了“无限猴子定理”，并为观众提供了观察随机生成文本的可能性。

• 正面观点2：有技术背景的用户对项目背后的编程实现表示赞赏，认为在技术层面上实现3000只“猴子”的模拟具有挑战性，并且是对计算资源和编程能力的一次展示。有用户提到，这样的项目可以作为编程和算法教学的案例。

• 批评观点1：部分用户认为该项目缺乏实际意义，纯粹是噱头，浪费计算资源。有评论指出，随机生成的文本几乎不可能产生有意义的文学作品，因此项目更多的是一种行为艺术，而非严肃的科学实验。

• 批评观点2：有用户质疑项目的原创性，认为此类模拟早已有之，并无新意。他们提到，类似的随机文本生成器和猴子打字模拟在互联网上并不少见，项目的独特性不足。

• 中立观点：一些用户持中立态度，认为该项目虽然不具备实际应用价值，但在创意和娱乐性方面有一定意义。他们提到，项目可以作为一个有趣的消遣，但不应被视为严肃的科学研究。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：项目是否具有实际意义和原创性是主要的争议点。部分用户认为其纯粹是娱乐性质的噱头，而另一些用户则对其技术实现和创意表示赞赏。

• 相关评论：有用户提到与该项目相关的前置讨论和类似项目，如“无限猴子定理”的实际应用和理论探讨，这为当前项目的理解提供了背景知识。

• 技术细节：一些用户对项目的技术细节进行了讨论，包括如何有效地模拟3000只猴子的打字行为，以及如何处理和展示随机生成的文本数据。这些讨论为项目的技术实现提供了更深入的理解。

43860993.article_content:
Making of Monkeys.zip (PART ONE)
May 1, 2025
It’s been one month since the
launch
of monkeys.zip. In that time, we’ve gathered over
11,000 monkeys
, which have written over
6 billion words
- completing well over
75%
of the words in Shakespeare’s works. In fact, they’ve
recently finished
writing every four-letter word!
While the initial hype has died down to a small trickle, the monkeys are still typing just as hard as ever, and I figured it’d be a good time to talk about how I built the site. If this part doesn’t interest you, check out
PART TWO
where I talk all about the monkey names!
Tech Stack
Backend & Database:
Supabase
Frontend Library:
LitHTML
3D Library:
Three.JS
Blog:
Astro
This is a relatively small list of technologies - as I tend to make as much as possible from scratch on my side projects, out of stubbornness. In this project, for example, I made a state management library called
StateFarm
. It’s awful, don’t use it.
Simulation Architecture
The more interesting stuff is how the backend simulation all comes together - it’s built as a loosely coupled pipeline with four main steps:
Ticks
The first important design decision comes with the concept of
Ticks
. The backend produces data in
15-second long
batches. The above pipeline runs every 15 seconds, producing 15 seconds worth of monkey-text. This interval length was chosen as a tradeoff between reducing runtime of each step, making errors easier to retry and recover from, and spreading out DB load into smaller chunks, while reducing server <—> client bandwidth and requests.
Step One  (generateTick)
Every 15 seconds, a cronjob calls a
generateTick
function - which has only one job - which is to put a new tick row in the
ticks
table.
Tick ID
Start Time
Seed
Status
1234
04:13:25
wn9837xw9873v
NEW
And that’s all it does! Keeping this step so simple and infallible is crucial to the reliability of later steps. If they fail, or there’s a huge data loss, everything can be rebuilt or retried as needed, as long as we have an entry in this table.
Step Two  (generateTickText)
When a new tick is added to this table, the
generateTickText
is called via a WebHook. This function has the job of generating the text for each monkey for that 15-second tick.
We use
sfc32
to deterministically generate random numbers based on the seed, which is the tick seed, merged with the monkey seed. This strategy allows a very deterministic random monkey text generator, that can execute both server-side and client-side.
note
I struggled with this for a while, internally debating if I should instead generate the text in a more random way, only on the server. It would feel more philosophically pure for the data to be ‘truly’ random. The downside of that is increased bandwidth (sending 150 bytes per monkey, vs a 24 byte seed).
Technically, due to the
pigeon-hole principle
, there are far less monkey-tick-seeds than there are 15-second monkey expositions. However, we can work on introducing a greater random space once we expend the existing one (which provides 2^128 states and will last for decades)
Once the text is generated, we drop it into a Storage bucket. This isn’t strictly necessary, but I like the transparency. For debugging or investigation purposes, it’s nice to be able to browse all the text that monkeys have written, without having to regenerate it.
Step Three (processTick)
When the text is dropped into Storage, another WebHook is called, which combs through the text and searches for matches against a dictionary. It builds an immense batch update do a number of Tables in our database
monkey_words
- Source of truth for every (valid) word every monkey has written
word_counts_cache
- Faster for lookups of a given word (EG “monkey” has appeared 100 times)
monkey_items
- Any items a monkey is earned is granted to this table
Step Four (Archive)
A more recent addition has been a separate cleanup script which runs on a cron job - the purpose of which is to archive old, short words from the
monkey_words
table and place them into a
monkey_words_archived
table - which drastically speeds up reads on
monkey_words
(which started slowing down at several billion rows).
Other Backend Things
The grid of monkeys is labeled into chunks of 64x64 - which hold almost no value, except for creating a minimum query size for monkeys while scrolling through the app - and allowing me to cache these chunks in Redis. During normal traffic, it’s actually slower (by over 100 ms) to fetch the cached result from Redis than just query the DB for it - but in the early days when the application was being battered by reddit, it was a lifesaver to be able to render the monkeys without the database needing to be responsive.
There’s still a fair amount of optimization that remains to be done. Now that we’re getting into the ‘diminishing returns’ portion of this project, I’d love to speed the monkey typing up, so that we can start carving through the 6 and 7 letter words, but that will require some further architectu

data.title: Why I'm getting off US tech
data.author: NickDouglas
data.article_summary: 文章作者巴黎·马克思（Paris Marx）讨论了为何他试图尽可能脱离对美国科技的依赖。文章指出，美国科技巨头如亚马逊、Facebook、Twitter和谷歌等公司已经堕落，平台质量下降，服务主要为公司利润最大化。这些公司与特朗普政府结盟，通过逃避税收和规避监管来维护自身利益，并威胁其他国家。作者认为，全球对美国科技的依赖是几十年来政策和市场主导的结果，而现在这些公司和美国政府的霸权行为正引发担忧，包括可能切断云服务等。作者呼吁各国政府采取数字主权策略，开发替代方案，并表示自己正在寻找非美国科技公司的数字服务替代品。尽管完全脱离美国科技并不现实，但他认为应采取行动应对美国科技公司的霸权。

不同观点：
• WorldPeas认为目前没有能够替代Macbook和iPhone的设备。他指出，这些设备在电池寿命、稳定性和性能方面具有优势，并且苹果的生态系统能够避免现代代码中的一些缺陷。他还提到，欧盟若想实现技术主权，不能仅依赖Linux，而需要与科技巨头合作。

• bigyabai对WorldPeas的观点持批评态度，认为其一边宣称寻求替代品一边继续使用苹果产品的行为自相矛盾。他通过讽刺“Boycott Amazon”贴纸却使用免费Prime shipping的例子，质疑这种立场的不一致性。

补充讨论：
• WorldPeas强调了苹果设备在技术性能和生态系统上的优势，认为这是其他操作系统（如Linux）无法比拟的。
• bigyabai则关注行为与言论的一致性问题，质疑那些声称要抵制或寻找替代品的人却在继续使用苹果产品的人的立场。
• 争议的焦点在于是否真的没有合适的替代品，以及在寻求技术主权的过程中，是否必须依赖科技巨头的产品。

这两种观点反映了在技术选择上的实用主义与理想主义之间的张力，以及个人选择与政治立场之间的潜在冲突。

At least as much as feasibly possible

In January, we watched Donald Trump be inaugurated as president for the second time, but there was something new: the billionaires of Silicon Valley
had a front row seat
. They’d funneled
hundreds of millions
of dollars into Trump’s campaign, then
millions more
into his inauguration fund. The tech titans made it clear they were aligned with his agenda as they sought to evade taxes and regulations in the United States, and hoped to use the administration’s leverage to bully other countries into backing off too.
That alliance became necessary because the old, naive narratives about the widespread benefits and better future being ushered in by Silicon Valley are long dead. The platforms we use have been continually degraded to serve the bottom lines of the companies that run them. Amazon is
full of poor-quality goods
, Facebook is
flooded with AI slop
, Twitter is
a right-wing cesspool
, Google sacrificed its trusted reputation for
confidently incorrect AI Overviews
, Microsoft is forcing generative AI on its clients, and the list goes on.
Our dependence on US tech isn’t the product of the past few months. It’s been
a decades-long project
, built on the false notions that digital technology had to be left to the private sector and that governments had limited power to shape it within their jurisdictions. Those assertions were crafted to benefit not just the US tech industry, but the global power of the United States itself. As its tech companies dominated markets around the world, they not only grew larger and became more profitable, but the influence of the US government expanded along with it.
For a while, that didn’t seem to be too much of a problem. The industry was surrounded with optimistic narratives and it was growing so quickly that crumbs could be thrown to other countries to keep them from questioning the unfavorable deal they’d tacitly accepted. But as it’s come under threat and seeks to defend the power it’s accrued, we’re seeing the consequences of that trade off.
Silicon Valley is enlisting Trump in its war against higher taxes
Paris Marx
·
Feb 24
Read full story
Countries are being
threatened with tariffs
for applying digital services taxes and enforcing regulations that seek to make foreign tech companies align with local rules and values. The United States is restricting chip exports not just to China, but even to countries that
thought they were its close allies
. Most recently, fears have been growing that US cloud services like Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure — which so many companies and governments have come to depend on — could even
be shut off
if Trump’s trade war deepens.
After watching the industry’s
embrace of the extreme right
and how that enabled Trump’s aggression toward so many around the world, I’ve had enough.
A proper response to the dominance of US tech firms and the belligerence of the US government won’t come through individual actions; it requires governments in Europe, Canada, Brazil, and many other parts of the world to
strategize and deploy serious resources
to develop an alternative. That’s why I’ve been arguing for them to
take digital sovereignty seriously
, and particularly a form of it that challenges the foundations and incentives that modern Silicon Valley was built on.
But the more I see what the Trump administration and the tech billionaires are doing, the more I feel I can’t wait for governments to get their acts together. For the past several weeks, I’ve started identifying digital services from companies outside the United States and testing them to see if I can find reasonable alternatives to the US platforms and companies I currently rely on.
The United States has gone rogue. There must be consequences.
Paris Marx
·
Mar 4
Read full story
There are still places where reasonable alternatives are hard to find, or where the only ones available are made by coders for their own — the type of thing I can never recommend to a wider audience. But even with that said, I’ve found there are more options than I expected — and many of them don’t require the compromises I thought would be necessary. There is always the friction of switching and getting used to something new, but that honestly doesn’t take long to get over.
I know I’m not going to be able to fully disconnect from the US tech economy. Some platforms will be harder to give up than others, particularly when I need to use popular social media platforms to share my work. I’m also not getting rid of my Macbook and iPhone, at least for now, and even when I do find good alternatives, some of them are still on AWS or another US cloud service.
